title: feat: Add image/screenshot support — clipboard paste, drag-drop, and file path input
body:
## Problem

SoulForge currently has **no way to send images to the AI model**. There is no clipboard paste (Ctrl+V/Cmd+V), no drag-and-drop, no file path reference, and no base64 encoding mechanism for images.

This is a significant gap because:

1. **All major LLM providers SoulForge supports have vision capabilities** — Claude (Anthropic), GPT-4o (OpenAI), Gemini (Google), and Grok (xAI) all accept image inputs natively.
2. **Competitors already support this** — Claude Code supports Ctrl+V clipboard paste, drag-and-drop, and file path references for images. Other CLI tools like Hermes Agent also support multimodal vision.
3. **Common use cases are blocked:**
   - Pasting a screenshot of a UI bug and asking "fix this layout"
   - Sharing a design mockup and asking for implementation
   - Showing error screenshots from browsers/mobile devices
   - Referencing architecture diagrams or wireframes
   - Sharing terminal output screenshots when text copy isn't possible

## Current Behavior

- Pasting an image via Ctrl+V in the InputBox does nothing (only text paste works)
- No `/image` or `/screenshot` slash command exists
- No `--image` flag in headless mode
- The 86 documented slash commands and 35 tools have zero image-related functionality
- The Vercel AI SDK used by SoulForge (`useChat`) supports `image` content parts, but SoulForge doesn't utilize this

## Expected Behavior

### Interactive Mode (TUI)
- **Clipboard paste**: Ctrl+V / Cmd+V detects image data in clipboard, converts to base64, and attaches as an `image` content block alongside the text message
- **File path reference**: `/image path/to/screenshot.png` or inline `@image:path/to/file.png` syntax to attach local image files
- **Visual indicator**: Show a thumbnail or `[📷 image attached]` badge in the input area when an image is queued

### Headless Mode
- **Flag**: `soulforge --headless --image path/to/screenshot.png "What's wrong with this layout?"`
- **Stdin**: Support piped image data or base64-encoded image input

### Supported Formats
- PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP (standard formats supported by all vision-capable models)
- Automatic format detection from magic bytes or file extension

## Technical Context

- SoulForge uses the **Vercel AI SDK** which already supports `ImagePart` in message content arrays
- The `useChat` hook and `streamText`/`generateText` APIs accept `{ type: 'image', image: base64Data }` content parts
- The InputBox component (OpenTUI-based) would need clipboard event handling for image data
- Provider capability detection may be needed — not all models support vision (e.g., Haiku 3.5 doesn't)
- Image data should be excluded from compaction/context summaries (store as reference, not inline base64 in summaries)

## Environment

- SoulForge v2.0.0
- macOS / Linux terminal (iTerm2, Kitty, WezTerm, Alacritty, etc.)
- All LLM providers tested (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google)

## Additional Notes

This is arguably the most impactful missing feature for developer workflows. Visual debugging (showing the AI what something looks like) is one of the highest-value use cases for multimodal models, and SoulForge's terminal-native approach shouldn't be a barrier — clipboard APIs work in terminal applications, and the AI SDK already supports the wire format.

title: In-app restart after update fails on compiled installs with Module not found '/$bunfs/root/soulforge.js'
body:
## Summary
After an in-app update, choosing restart can fail on compiled installs with:

```
error: Module not found "/$bunfs/root/soulforge.js"
```

## Why this happens
SoulForge restart currently respawns using `process.argv[0]` and `process.argv.slice(1)` in `src/index.tsx`.

For Bun compiled binaries, normal runtime argv looks like:

```json
{
  "execPath": "/path/to/real/binary",
  "argv": ["bun", "/$bunfs/root/<entry>", "..."]
}
```

So the current restart logic effectively replays:

```
bun /$bunfs/root/soulforge.js
```

which fails in a fresh process because that embedded bundle path is not a real on-disk module target.

## Relevant code
- `src/index.tsx:108-123`
  - `hardRestart()` uses `const args = process.argv.slice(1)`
  - then `Bun.spawn([argv0, ...args], ...)`
- `src/boot.tsx:5`
  - CLI parsing assumes real user args begin at `process.argv.slice(2)`

## Repro
### Minimal Bun repro
Compiled Bun binary runtime argv:

```json
{
  "execPath": "/private/tmp/sf-repro/argv-repro",
  "argv": ["bun", "/$bunfs/root/argv-repro"]
}
```

Replaying the restart shape:

```
bun '/$bunfs/root/argv-repro'
```

produces:

```
error: Module not found "/$bunfs/root/argv-repro"
```

### SoulForge symptom
The same replay shape with the SoulForge entrypoint:

```
bun '/$bunfs/root/soulforge.js'
```

produces:

```
error: Module not found "/$bunfs/root/soulforge.js"
```

## Expected
After upgrade, restart should relaunch the actual binary path, not the Bun internal bundle entry.

## Likely fix
Use `process.execPath` for the executable and only pass real user args, i.e. the equivalent of `process.argv.slice(2)` for compiled installs, instead of replaying the embedded `/$bunfs/...` argv entry.

I also hit this through a Homebrew-installed setup where the app updates and then fails on restart, but the core bug appears to be the compiled Bun restart path above.

title: navigate tool does not work for .luau files even with luau-lsp installed
body:
Steps to reproduce

Install luau-lsp via /lsp install or manually. The binary at ~/.soulforge/lsp-servers/bin/luau-lsp version 1.68.1 works and responds to --version. Open a .luau file in a project and call navigate(action: "definition", symbol: "someFunction") on a symbol defined in that file.

Expected

navigate returns the file and line of the definition.

Actual

navigate returns "No definition backend available for this file type."

Root cause

The server registry in SoulForge maps file extensions to LSP backends. .luau is not in that mapping. Lua (.lua) is supported but Luau (.luau) is a different language with its own LSP server. luau-lsp handles both .lua and .luau files, so the fix is adding ".luau" alongside ".lua" in the LSP server registration for luau-lsp.

Context

The project uses Rojo with Luau as the primary language. .luau files are the standard extension. This blocks all LSP-backed tools (navigate, analyze, rename) for the entire codebase. soul_grep and read still work because they don't use LSP.

Additional info

Installed at ~/.soulforge/lsp-servers/bin/luau-lsp (version 1.68.1). Also present in lsp-versions.json as installed 2026-06-23. Server starts fine when invoked directly.

The server-registry.ts file is the likely location for the fix. Adding ".luau" to the file extension list for the luau-lsp entry should resolve it.

title: Memory embeddings bypass SoulForge providers: embeddingModel strings resolve to Vercel AI Gateway, then silently fall back to offline
Model fallback never fires on HTTP 429 when the response body doesn't literally say "429" or "rate limit"
body:
I use `modelFallback` to fail over between two accounts of the same OpenAI-compatible provider when one runs out of quota. The provider (Sakana API) answers with HTTP **429** and this body:

```json
{"error":{"message":"Prepaid credit balance is exhausted. Add credits at ...","type":"usage_limit_reached"}}
```

Instead of retrying and swapping to the fallback model, the turn fails immediately.

The transient check only ever looks at error message text. The string under test is built by `causeChain`, which concatenates `name: message` down the cause chain ([useChat.ts:4333](https://github.com/proxysoul/soulforge/blob/8ae117e6045cd2da1f029173343cf602b84427d6/src/hooks/useChat.ts#L4333)) — the HTTP status code never makes it into that string. The classifier itself ([useChat.ts:3488](https://github.com/proxysoul/soulforge/blob/8ae117e6045cd2da1f029173343cf602b84427d6/src/hooks/useChat.ts#L3488)):

```ts
const isTransient =
  /overloaded|529|429|rate.?limit|too many requests|503|502|timeout|.../i.test(chain);
```

The AI SDK's `APICallError.message` carries the response body's message, and this particular body contains none of those tokens — so a textbook rate-limit response gets classified as permanent and the fallback chain never fires. The same message-only assumption shows up again at [useChat.ts:3771](https://github.com/proxysoul/soulforge/blob/8ae117e6045cd2da1f029173343cf602b84427d6/src/hooks/useChat.ts#L3771).

Checking `statusCode` on the error object (and perhaps the OpenAI-style `error.type`, e.g. `usage_limit_reached`) alongside the regex would make fallback work for any provider regardless of how it phrases quota errors.

soulforge 2.20.23 (npm), Linux x64.

title: Custom provider reasoning.effort sends reasoning_effort and reasoning together — strictly-validating backends reject the request
body:
With a custom OpenAI-compatible provider configured as `"reasoning": { "effort": "xhigh" }`, every request against the Sakana API fails with:

```
Pass either `reasoning` (nested object) or `reasoning_effort` (flat field), not both.
```

That comes from here, working as designed ([reasoning-fetch.ts:23-26](https://github.com/proxysoul/soulforge/blob/8ae117e6045cd2da1f029173343cf602b84427d6/src/core/llm/providers/reasoning-fetch.ts#L23-L26)):

```ts
if (effort && effort !== "off") {
  body.reasoning_effort = effort;
  body.reasoning = { effort };
}
```

The comment above explains the intent — cover both the current flat spec and the older nested one some routers still want — and lenient backends do just ignore the extra field. But a backend that validates strictly rejects the request outright, and `effort` gives no way to pick one style.

My workaround is to skip `effort` and inject the field manually with `"reasoning": { "extraParams": { "reasoning_effort": "xhigh" } }`, which works because `extraParams` is merged after that branch. An explicit injection-style option (flat / nested / both), or defaulting to flat-only for `/chat/completions` with "both" as a compat fallback, would make strict backends usable without the workaround.

title: Add OpenCode session import support (SQLite → Empryo JSONL)
body:
Empryo already supports importing sessions from Claude Code and Codex, it would be a natural addition to support **OpenCode** as well, allowing users migrating from OpenCode to Empryo to retain their full session history.

---

## OpenCode session storage

OpenCode stores all session data in a **SQLite database**:

| Platform | Path |
|---|---|
| Linux | `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db` |
| macOS | `~/Library/Application Support/opencode/opencode.db` |
| Windows | `%APPDATA%/opencode/opencode.db` |

---

## Database schema (tables relevant to sessions)

### `session`

| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `TEXT PK` | Session UUID |
| `project_id` | `TEXT` | FK → `project.id` |
| `workspace_id` | `TEXT` | FK → `workspace.id` |
| `parent_id` | `TEXT` | Parent session (for resumed sessions) |
| `slug` | `TEXT` | Human-readable short ID |
| `directory` | `TEXT` | Project working directory |
| `path` | `TEXT` | Full session path |
| `title` | `TEXT` | Session title |
| `version` | `TEXT` | OpenCode version |
| `share_url` | `TEXT` | Shared session URL |
| `summary_additions` | `INTEGER` | Lines added |
| `summary_deletions` | `INTEGER` | Lines deleted |
| `summary_files` | `INTEGER` | Files changed |
| `summary_diffs` | `TEXT` | JSON diff summary |
| `metadata` | `TEXT` | Arbitrary JSON metadata |
| `cost` | `REAL` | Total cost in USD |
| `tokens_input` | `INTEGER` | Total input tokens |
| `tokens_output` | `INTEGER` | Total output tokens |
| `tokens_reasoning` | `INTEGER` | Reasoning tokens |
| `tokens_cache_read` | `INTEGER` | Cache read tokens |
| `tokens_cache_write` | `INTEGER` | Cache write tokens |
| `revert` | `TEXT` | Revert data |
| `permission` | `TEXT` | Permission mode used |
| `agent` | `TEXT` | Agent type |
| `model` | `TEXT` | LLM model used |
| `time_created` | `INTEGER` | Unix timestamp |
| `time_updated` | `INTEGER` | Unix timestamp |
| `time_compacting` | `INTEGER` | Last compact timestamp |
| `time_archived` | `INTEGER` | Archive timestamp |

### `session_message`

| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `TEXT PK` | Message UUID |
| `session_id` | `TEXT` | FK → `session.id` |
| `type` | `TEXT` | `user`, `assistant`, or `tool` |
| `seq` | `INTEGER` | Order within session |
| `time_created` | `INTEGER` | Unix timestamp |
| `time_updated` | `INTEGER` | Unix timestamp |
| `data` | `TEXT` | Full message JSON content |

### `session_input`

| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `TEXT PK` | Input UUID |
| `session_id` | `TEXT` | FK → `session.id` |
| `prompt` | `TEXT` | User prompt text |
| `delivery` | `TEXT` | Delivery mode |
| `admitted_seq` | `INTEGER` | Admission sequence |
| `promoted_seq` | `INTEGER` | Promotion sequence |
| `time_created` | `INTEGER` | Unix timestamp |

---

## Proposed data mapping

| OpenCode | Empryo |
|---|---|
| `session.title` | Session title |
| `session.directory` | Project directory path |
| `session.model` | LLM model identifier |
| `session.agent` | Agent type |
| `session.time_created` | Session creation time |
| `session.time_updated` | Last activity time |
| `session.cost` | Total cost (USD) |
| `session.tokens_input` | Input token count |
| `session.tokens_output` | Output token count |
| `session.tokens_reasoning` | Reasoning token count |
| `session.summary_additions` | Lines added |
| `session.summary_deletions` | Lines deleted |
| `session.summary_files` | Files changed |
| `session.summary_diffs` | Diff metadata |
| `session_message` (ordered by `seq`) | Conversation messages (JSONL) |
| `session_input` | User prompts with timestamps |

---

## Detection

OpenCode can be auto-detected by scanning for `opencode.db` at the platform-specific paths listed above. The SQLite database is always present when OpenCode has been used at least once.

---

## Suggested UX

A command same to the existing `/import` flow for Claude Code:

This would:

1. Detect `opencode.db` at the standard location
2. List all available sessions with title, date, project, model, and token count
3. Let the user select sessions to import (checkbox picker)
4. Convert and write sessions to `~/.empryo/sessions/` as standard Empryo JSONL
5. Preserve all messages ordered by sequence, with user prompts, assistant responses, and tool calls mapped appropriately

title: [BUG] Conversation crashes when context exceeds 1MB - no fallback or recovery path
body: ## Overview I'm running into a hard crash whenever the conversation context grows too large. The application simply stops responding with a raw error message, leaving no way to recover or continue the session. This happens repeatedly during longer work sessions. ## What Happens During extended conversations especially when working through large technical audits the system suddenly fails with this error: ``` Codex exec exited with code 1: Reading prompt from stdin... Error: turn/start: turn/start failed: Input exceeds the maximum length of 1048576 characters. (code -32602) data: {"input_error_code":"input_too_large","max_chars":1048576,"actual_chars":1049907} ``` The actual payload sometimes overshoots by just ~1.3KB, other times by nearly 200KB. Either way, the result is the same: the session dies instantly. ## Why This Is Problematic I'm working on complex, multi-turn tasks like auditing database schemas, reviewing RLS policies, and analyzing SECURITY DEFINER functions. These workflows naturally accumulate a lot of context. When the limit is hit: - There's no warning before the crash - No graceful degradation or prompt compression - No option to save/export the current state - The agent makes no attempt to retry or adapt - All progress since the last checkpoint is lost Essentially, the 1MB limit acts as a wall with no ramp-up, no safety net. ## What I'd Expect Instead Ideally, the system should detect an oversized context proactively and handle it gracefully. Some possibilities: 1. **Auto-compress old turns** — drop or summarize earlier messages to make room 2. **Checkpoint + resume** — let me export the current state and start fresh with context preserved 3. **Smart chunking** — split the prompt internally across multiple backend calls 4. **Early warning** — notify me before hitting the limit with options to reduce or continue Right now, there's zero of this. It's binary: you're under the limit and things work, or you're over and everything breaks. ## Environment - **Platform**: Empryo Desktop on Arch Linux - **Provider**: Codex with gpt-5.6-terra - **Workflow**: Extended technical sessions (database auditing, schema analysis) - **Typical failure point**: Mid-task, during large context injections

title: [Feature] Enhance file explorer with Git status color coding for improved workflow visibility
body:
## Overview
Add Git-aware color coding to the file explorer tree, so users can identify file status (modified, staged, untracked, etc.) at a glance without running `git status` separately.

## Problem / Current State
Currently, all files appear in uniform light gray/off-white text, with no distinction:
- No differentiation between tracked and untracked files
- No indication of modified vs. unchanged files
- No visual feedback on staged vs. unstaged changes
- No highlighting of newly created or deleted files

The design stays clean, but it forces a round-trip to the terminal just to know the real state of the repo.

## Proposed Enhancement
Apply color coding based on Git status, similar to VS Code / GitLens.

| Git Status | Suggested Color | Use Case |
|---|---|---|
| **Untracked** | Bright accent (green/cyan) | New files/folders not yet added to Git |
| **Modified** (unstaged) | Warning tone (yellow/orange) | Files with unstaged changes |
| **Staged** | Success tone (blue/green) | Changes added via `git add` |
| **Ignored** | Dimmed/gray opacity | Files matching `.gitignore` |
| **Deleted** | Subtle red/dashed | Removed files still tracked |
| **Clean** | Default neutral gray | No pending changes |

### Optional Enhancements
- Small icons next to filenames (✓ staged, ✏️ modified, + new, ⨯ deleted)
- Tooltip showing diff stats (lines added/removed) on hover
- Badge showing total count of modified/untracked files
- Toggle to enable/disable Git colors (for users who prefer a minimal UI)

## Example

**Before:**
```
docs/
├── package-lock.json
├── package.json
├── README.md
├── rls-report.html
└── schema.json
```
No status info visible.

**After:**
```
docs/
├── package-lock.json   [staged ✓]
├── package.json        [modified ✏️]
├── README.md           [clean]
├── rls-report.html     [untracked +]
└── schema.json         [clean]
```
Instant visibility into what matters.

## Benefits
1. **Faster context switching** — see what's changed without leaving the editor
2. **Reduced friction** — no need to open a terminal just to check file status
3. **Better commit hygiene** — visually confirm what you're about to stage
4. **Fewer mistakes** — catch uncommitted changes before switching branches or closing the project

## Implementation Notes
- Should integrate with existing Git detection (Empryo already tracks repos)
- Colors should respect the user's theme (light/dark mode)
- Performance impact should be negligible (Git status is cached)
- Could ship incrementally: colors first, icons/toggle later

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Untracked, modified, staged, ignored, deleted, and clean files each have a visually distinct color
- [ ] Colors respect the active light/dark theme
- [ ] No noticeable performance regression on a medium-sized repo
- [ ] (Optional) Toggle to disable the feature

title: [BUG] Memory store deletes -wal/-shm and renames the DB to .corrupt-<ts> before logging why — network-mounted workspace reports only "bridge init failed: EINVAL … rename"
body:
## Summary

Pointing the desktop app at a network-mounted workspace makes `empryo-bridge` fail at startup with

```
bridge init failed: EINVAL: invalid argument, rename '/Volumes/dell-ml.localhost/.empryo/memory.db' -> '/Volumes/dell-ml.localhost/.empryo/memory.db.corrupt-ms6cphxl'
```

The database is **not** corrupt. SQLite simply cannot be opened on that filesystem, and the memory store's recovery path reacts by (1) deleting `-wal`/`-shm` and (2) renaming the DB aside — both *before* the real SQLite error is ever printed. The rename is what fails, so the only thing the user sees is an `EINVAL` about a file they never asked to move, and the actual cause is swallowed.

## Environment

- Desktop: Empryo.app 3.5.5-beta on macOS 27.0 (arm64), `Contents/Resources/empryo-bridge`
- CLI/TUI: empryo 3.5.5-beta on Linux x64 (the machine that owns the files)
- Workspace: macOS `webdavfs` mount of a remote Linux `$HOME`
  `http://dell-ml.localhost:9876/ on /Volumes/dell-ml.localhost (webdav, nodev, noexec, nosuid)`
  served by `rclone serve webdav :sftp,ssh='ssh admin@remote-host': --addr 127.0.0.1:9876 --vfs-cache-mode writes`

## Root cause

The bridge's cwd was the mount root, so the project state dir resolved to `<mount>/.empryo` and the memory store tried to open a SQLite DB living on WebDAV. From the 3.5.5-beta bundle (minified, reformatted):

```js
try {
  let U;
  for (let Z = 0; Z < 3 && F === null; Z++)
    try { F = E() } catch (O) { if (U = O, q === ":memory:") throw O; Bun.sleepSync(50 * (Z + 1)) }
  if (F === null) throw U
} catch (U) {
  if (q === ":memory:") throw U;
  try { F?.close() } catch {}
  F = null;
  for (let Z of ["-wal", "-shm"]) try { rmSync(q + Z, { force: !0 }) } catch {}   // (1) destructive
  try {
    F = E();
    process.stderr.write(`[memory] ${p} had a torn WAL (${U.message}) — recovered from the main file\n`)
  } catch {
    let Z = `${q}.corrupt-${Date.now().toString(36)}`;
    renameSync(q, Z);                                                             // (2) throws EINVAL here
    process.stderr.write(`[memory] ${p} was unreadable (${U.message}) — moved to ${Z}, salvaging what's readable\n`)
  }
}
```

Why each step fails on this mount:

- `new Database(...)` / `PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL` cannot succeed: WAL needs a `-shm` mapping shared between processes on the *same host* ("All processes using a database must be on the same host computer; WAL does not work over a network filesystem" — sqlite.org/wal.html). Nothing here is a data problem.
- `renameSync` on macOS `webdavfs` returns `EINVAL`, so the recovery path throws out of the constructor and the bridge never comes up. The `process.stderr.write` that names the real SQLite error sits *after* the rename, so it never runs.

## Two defects

1. **The diagnosis is destroyed before it is reported.** The stderr line explaining the real failure is emitted after the mutation it describes. Any failure in `rm(-wal/-shm)` or `rename` replaces a precise SQLite message ("disk I/O error" / "unable to open database file") with an unrelated filesystem errno. Log first, mutate second.
2. **An open failure is treated as corruption unconditionally.** `SQLITE_CANTOPEN` / `SQLITE_IOERR_SHMOPEN` / `EPERM` / a locked file / a read-only mount are all "the environment is wrong", not "the bytes are bad" — and each one currently costs the user their `-wal`/`-shm` and then their DB file. In my case the DB being quarantined was the *live global* `~/.empryo/memory.db` of another machine, open at that moment by its own `em` process (`integrity_check: ok`, 31 tables). Only webdavfs's refusal to rename kept it in place; on an `rclone mount`/`sshfs` workspace the rename succeeds and the other host's memory silently disappears — and the unconditional `-wal`/`-shm` delete lands on a DB another process has open.

## Reproduce

1. Mount any remote dir on macOS via WebDAV (`rclone serve webdav <remote> --addr 127.0.0.1:9876` + `mount_webdav`) or FUSE (`rclone mount`, `sshfs`).
2. Open that mount as the workspace in Empryo desktop (or run `em` with cwd inside it).
3. Bridge init fails with the `EINVAL … rename` above; with a FUSE mount instead, the rename succeeds and `memory.db.corrupt-<base36>` appears while the real cause is still unreported.

## Suggested fix

- Reorder: write the `[memory] … was unreadable (<sqlite error>)` line **before** any `rm`/`rename`, and wrap both mutations so their errno is reported *in addition to* the original error, not instead of it.
- Only quarantine on codes that actually mean corruption (`SQLITE_CORRUPT`, `SQLITE_NOTADB`); for `SQLITE_CANTOPEN`/`SQLITE_IOERR*`/`EACCES`/`EPERM`/`EROFS`, fail loudly with a message naming the filesystem instead of touching user data.
- Detect a non-local state dir up front (macOS `webdav`/`nfs`/`smbfs`/`fuse`, Linux `statfs` magic) and refuse with something actionable — "Empryo's state DB can't live on a network mount; open a local folder" — rather than entering the corruption path. Falling back to a local state dir (or `:memory:`) would make network-mounted workspaces merely slow instead of unusable.
- Never delete `-wal`/`-shm` for a DB that another process may hold; a torn-WAL recovery should at least gate on the DB being local and unlocked.

## Evidence

- Mac side: `empryo-bridge` cwd `/Volumes/dell-ml.localhost` (`lsof -a -p <pid> -d cwd`), mount line as quoted above.
- Linux side, same instant: `sqlite3 ~/.empryo/memory.db 'pragma integrity_check'` → `ok`; no `*.corrupt-*` produced; the traversal left `._*` AppleDouble sidecars through `~/.empryo`.
- `ms6cphxl` in the error is `Date.now().toString(36)`, which is what identifies the code path above.

Running the same 3.5.5-beta build (Linux desktop AppImage) directly on the machine that owns the files, with the same `/home/<user>` workspace, brings the bridge up immediately — the only variable is the filesystem.

title: MiniMax: drop dead reasoning_effort injection; decide on Anthropic-compatible endpoint + region select
body:
## Context

Split out of #153. That PR targets the old flat SoulForge layout (`src/core/llm/...`, `mintlify-docs/`) and cannot be merged into the Empryo monorepo, and parts of it are factually wrong against the live MiniMax catalog. This issue tracks the one part that is genuinely correct and the follow-up that still needs a decision.

## Done (landing in the next Empryo version)

MiniMax no longer gets an OpenAI-compat `reasoning_effort` body injected.

- `packages/core/src/llm/compat-reasoning.ts` — removed `minimax` from `COMPAT_PROVIDERS`.
- `packages/core/src/llm/provider-options.ts` — removed `/minimax-m[2-9]/` from the `compatReasoning` capability test.

Rationale: MiniMax's text API documents `thinking: { type: "adaptive" | "disabled" }` (plus `reasoning_split`), not `reasoning_effort`. Undocumented OpenAI params are ignored by that endpoint, so the injected key was dead weight on every MiniMax request. Thinking stays on by default for M3 over the OpenAI-compatible endpoint, so removing it is behaviour-neutral.

Verified: `bun test` over `reasoning-effort-style`, `new-providers`, `provider-options` and `forge-cache` — 141 pass. `getCompatReasoningBody("minimax/MiniMax-M3", { effort: "high" })` now returns `{}`.

## Open — Anthropic-compatible endpoint + region select

MiniMax docs mark the Anthropic-shaped endpoint as recommended, and models.dev now declares the provider as `api: https://api.minimax.io/anthropic/v1`, `npm: @ai-sdk/anthropic`. Empryo still routes through `vercel-minimax-ai-provider` (OpenAI-compatible, pinned at `^0.0.2`), and there is no way to pick the CN endpoint (`https://api.minimaxi.com/anthropic`) even though an account credential only validates against its own region.

Blocker before I switch transport: over the Anthropic endpoint, thinking is **off** by default for `MiniMax-M3` and must be requested with `thinking: { type: "adaptive" }`, while `provider-options.ts` gates `anthropicOptions` on `family === "claude"`. A naive swap to `createAnthropic` silently disables M3 reasoning. Migration therefore needs the MiniMax family wired into the Anthropic options path (thinking, prompt caching, `anthropic-beta` headers) rather than a one-line provider swap.

## Rejected from #153

- **M3 pricing `$0.6 in / $2.4 out`, cache read `$0.12`** — wrong. models.dev and OpenRouter both report `$0.30 / $1.20` with `$0.06` cache read for `MiniMax-M3`; `$0.6 / $2.4` is the highspeed tier. `apps/cli/src/stores/statusbar.ts` already carries the correct table (`minimax-m3: 0.3 / 1.2 / cacheRead 0.06`), verified 2026-07-09.
- **Trimming `fallbackModels` to M3 + M2.7** — MiniMax still lists `MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed`, `MiniMax-M2.5`, `MiniMax-M2.5-highspeed`, `MiniMax-M2.1`, `MiniMax-M2.1-highspeed` and `MiniMax-M2` as selectable SKUs. Dropping them would remove working models and their pricing rows.
- **Context windows** — already correct in `packages/core/src/llm/providers/minimax.ts` (M3 = 1,000,000, M2.x = 204,800).

title: Feature Request: Manual "Review" Mode Independent from `/loop`
body: ### Context The `/loop` command currently launches an autonomous review cycle that iterates until the work is validated and confirmed compliant with the user's original request. This works great as a fully automated flow, but there's currently no way to trigger this same review mechanism **manually**, outside of running a full `/loop`. ### Problem When there's a one-off doubt about work that's already been completed (an agent's output, generated code, etc.), there's no simple way to request a second opinion / verification from another model, without having to restart an entire work loop from scratch. ### Proposal Add a command (e.g. `/review` or `/verify`) that: - Spawns the same review process used internally by `/loop` - Can be triggered manually, at any point, on work that's already been done - Ideally uses a different model than the one that produced the work (for genuine cross-checking) - Verifies compliance against: - The user's original request - The rules defined in the project's memories - Returns a clear verdict (approved / non-compliant + explanation of the discrepancies) ### Use Cases - Quality check on demand for work done outside of `/loop` - Resolving a one-off doubt without restarting a full cycle - Getting verification from a different model to avoid a single model's bias toward its own output ### Value Adds confidence and flexibility: keeps the rigor of `/loop`, but lets you apply it selectively, on demand, without the time/token cost of a full cycle.

title: Crash with "Illegal instruction" on Windows x64 with Bun v1.3.14
body:
## Description

`empryo` crashes with an `Illegal instruction` panic when running on Windows x64 with Bun v1.3.14.

### Error

```text
Bun v1.3.14 (0d9b296a) Windows x64
Windows v.win10_cu
CPU: sse42 avx
Args:
Features: no_avx2

panic: Illegal instruction at address 0x7FF662BCF82C
panicked during a panic. Aborting.
```

### Environment

* **Bun:** v1.3.14 (`0d9b296a`)
* **OS:** Windows x64 (`win10_cu`)
* **CPU features:** SSE4.2, AVX
* **AVX2:** Not available (`no_avx2`)

### Actual Behavior

The process terminates with an `Illegal instruction` panic. The runtime then reports:

```text
panicked during a panic. Aborting.
```

### Expected Behavior

`empryo` should run normally on CPUs supporting SSE4.2 and AVX, even when AVX2 is unavailable.

## Summary

Please add proper Arabic right-to-left (RTL) text rendering to the **Empryo Desktop app**.

This request is specifically about display and text direction. It does **not** require translating or localizing the application UI.

## Motivation

Arabic prompts and model responses are currently difficult to read when they are rendered using a left-to-right layout. The problem becomes more noticeable in mixed content that combines Arabic with English words, numbers, punctuation, file paths, or inline code.

Supporting bidirectional text correctly would make the Desktop app much more usable for Arabic-speaking developers without requiring a broader localization effort.

## Requested behavior

- Detect Arabic/RTL text at an appropriate content-block or paragraph level and render it right-to-left with right alignment.
- Preserve natural ordering and punctuation in mixed Arabic and English content.

  - fenced and inline code
  - shell commands
  - file paths and URLs
  - diffs
  - editor and terminal output
- Ensure Markdown elements such as paragraphs, lists, headings, and blockquotes display correctly in Arabic.
- Keep text selection, cursor behavior, copying, and pasting predictable for RTL and mixed-direction content.

Where appropriate, standards-based direction handling such as `dir="auto"` at block boundaries and isolated bidirectional content could help avoid forcing one direction on an entire message.

This request is intentionally limited to the **Desktop app**.

Out of scope for this request:

- Arabic UI translation/localization
- Mirroring the entire application layout
- TUI or headless CLI support

The application controls and interface language can remain English; only user-authored and model-generated Arabic content needs correct RTL presentation.

- Arabic prompts and responses are right-aligned and read naturally from right to left in the Desktop app.
- Mixed Arabic/English paragraphs preserve the expected reading order.

title: T-CELLS-02 · edit_file writes through a read-only file
body:
> **T-CELL FIELD REPORT** · `T-CELLS-02` · Empryo `3.5.10-beta`
>
> _A file you marked read-only (chmod 444) is edited anyway, and the agent is told the edit succeeded._

### ⌁ spread

| macOS | Linux | Windows |
|---|---|---|
| ✗ | ✗ | · |

<sub>✗ reproduced · ✓ not reproduced · · not tested on this platform</sub>

### ⌁ exposure

Anyone who protects a file and then lets the agent work in that repo — generated code, a vendored lockfile, a config someone froze on purpose. The agent has no way to know the write was not supposed to be possible, so it goes on reasoning about a file it should not have touched. It needs no special mode: an ordinary `edit_file` in `--mode auto` does it.

### ⌁ culture — reproduce it

```bash
# in any repo, with a file the agent is allowed to see
printf 'original\n' > locked.txt && chmod 444 locked.txt
empryo --headless --mode auto 'change "original" to "changed" in locked.txt'
cat locked.txt   # -> changed

# or, from an Empryo checkout, as the T cell runs it:
bun qa/run.ts --seeds=edges/read-only-file --platforms=macos
```

### ⌁ assay — what was asserted, what came back

```
asserted: the file is unchanged after an edit_file against a 0444 target
got:      content replaced ("original" -> "changed"); the tool reported success to the model
also:     before the T-CELLS-01 fix the mode was reset to 0644 as well — that part is fixed
```

### ⌁ sequence — where it comes from

packages/base/src/platform/index.ts — `writeOnce()` writes a sibling temp file and `rename()`s it over the target. That is the correct shape for crash safety (a half-written file can never replace a good one), but POSIX `rename(2)` checks write permission on the **directory**, not on the file being replaced. The target's own mode is never consulted, so 0444 is not an obstacle. `edit_file`, `multi_edit` and every other caller of `atomicWriteFile` inherit the behaviour.

### ⌁ immunity — what guards it now

`edges/read-only-file` is a permanent seed in the T-cell thymus — it reproduces this on demand, on
every platform marked tested above. While the defect is open the seed reports as a *known issue*
rather than a failure, so it cannot mask a new regression; the day it passes, the patrol says so
out loud and the marker comes off.

### ⌁ treatment

Two defensible options, and it is a product decision rather than a patch. (1) Check `access(target, W_OK)` before writing and return a tool error the model can act on — an unattended agent then cannot write through a protection the user set deliberately. (2) Keep editor-like behaviour, where read-only is advisory, but say so in the tool result so the model knows the file was protected. What is not defensible is the current silence. The seed is marked as a known issue meanwhile, so it reports as known rather than masking new regressions.

---

<sub>Found by **Empryo T-Cells** — the project's own QA immune system: seeds describe what must
hold, killer cells execute them against the real product on macOS · Linux · Windows, and every
confirmed defect becomes a memory cell. Reproduce with `bun qa/run.ts --seeds=edges/read-only-file`.</sub>

title: 3.6.0-beta: auto-compaction can retain an oversized recent turn and hit provider char limit
body:
## Summary

On `3.6.0-beta`, a long tool-heavy conversation can still exceed the provider's request character limit before proactive compaction prevents the request.

The reactive recovery added for #142 works: Empryo recognizes the capacity error, compacts, and retries. However, the user still sees a fatal-looking mid-turn error/stall, and normal post-turn compaction can retain too much of one very large recent turn to reach its configured reset target.

## Environment

- Empryo Desktop `3.6.0-beta`
- macOS arm64
- Compaction strategy `v2`
- OpenAI-compatible proxy with a `1,048,576` character request limit

## Errors observed

```text
Request is 1,064,625 chars, over this provider's limit of 1,048,576
Request is 1,053,367 chars, over this provider's limit of 1,048,576
```

Both occurred during long turns containing large batches of `web_search`, `fetch_page`, and shell results. Empryo subsequently emitted `core-reset` with `reason:"compaction"` and continued, so this is not a failure of the reactive recovery itself.

## Reproduction pattern

1. Use a long existing conversation with multiple tool-heavy turns.
2. Run another long turn that accumulates many tool results before it completes.
3. The next intermediate model request grows past the provider's character limit.
4. The provider rejects the request; only then does the capacity-error recovery compact and retry.

The retention behavior is also visible after normal post-turn compaction:

- With `keepRecent: 4`, one automatic compaction retained `48` core messages and left the request at `508k/971k chars` (`52%`), despite a `resetThreshold` of `0.2`.
- In an earlier case, automatic compaction left `636,392` serialized characters (`68%`) because the large recent turn was retained.
- With `keepRecent: 2`, the next automatic compaction retained `4` core messages and reduced the request to `69k/971k chars` (`7%`).

## Expected behavior

Before every provider request within a turn, Empryo should check projected request capacity using both token and character limits and compact before sending an oversized request.

If a single recent turn prevents compaction from reaching `resetThreshold`, old tool-result bodies inside that retained turn should be summarized or pruned until the target is reached, or the UI should explicitly report that the reset target could not be met.

This is narrower than #142: that issue added recovery after an overflow response. This report concerns preventing the overflow request and ensuring post-turn compaction reaches a safe baseline.

## Verified workaround

```json
"compaction": {
  "strategy": "v2",
  "triggerThreshold": 0.3,
  "resetThreshold": 0.2,
  "keepRecent": 2,
  "maxToolResults": 30,
  "llmExtraction": true
}
```

After restarting and running a control turn, the automatic compaction completed successfully and left `902k chars` of request headroom.

title: matchPricing(): grok-4.5/4.6 silently fall through to the grok-4 row (output 2.5x high), claude-sonnet-5 lands on DEFAULT_PRICING, and the DeepSeek block predates the 2026-08-17 repricing
body:
Three things in `src/stores/statusbar.ts`. The second one is structural and will keep recurring, so it may be worth more than the price refresh.

## 1. `includes()` matching sends a new minor version to its old major-version row

`matchPricing()` sorts keys by length descending and then does `id.includes(key)`. The comment says this is so `claude-opus-4-6` wins over `claude-opus-4`, which it does. But the ordering only protects keys that are **longer**; a model newer than anything in the table falls through to the shortest prefix that still matches.

`grok-4.5` and `grok-4.6` are exactly that case. No longer key matches, so `"grok-4.5".includes("grok-4")` wins and both get the `grok-4` row:

| | table gives (`grok-4`) | actual ≤200k | error |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| input | $3 | $2 | 1.5× high |
| output | $15 | $6 | **2.5× high** |
| cacheRead | $0.75 | $0.30 (4.5) / $0.50 (4.6) | 1.5–2.5× high |

(Both double above a 200k prompt, which this table does not model for xAI — it does note it for Gemini Pro.)

The failure is silent and it is the wrong direction for a status bar: a user sees a number 2.5× too high and has no reason to doubt it. The same shape will hit `grok-3.x`, and any future `claude-opus-4-9`-style ID.

Two options, both cheap: require an exact key match and let the per-family heuristics below handle everything else (they already exist, and are already better — `claude-opus-5` currently resolves correctly *only* because it matches no key at all and lands on the `opus` heuristic), or keep `includes()` but require the match to end at a version boundary.

## 2. `claude-sonnet-5` matches nothing and lands on `DEFAULT_PRICING`

Same mechanism, milder: no `claude-sonnet-5` key exists, so `id.includes("sonnet")` returns `DEFAULT_PRICING` = `{3, 3.75, 0.3, 15}`, the Sonnet 4.x rates. Sonnet 5 currently lists at **$2 / $10** with a $0.20 cache read, so the status bar reads about 1.5× high on every Sonnet 5 session.

## 3. The DeepSeek block predates the 2026-08-17 repricing

The source comment says 2026-06-02. DeepSeek moved V4 to time-of-day billing on 2026-08-17. From the [pricing page](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/pricing/) (read 2026-08-24), per 1M tokens:

| | cache hit | input | output |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| v4-pro off-peak | 0.022 | 0.66 | 1.98 |
| v4-pro peak | 0.044 | 1.32 | 3.96 |
| v4-flash off-peak | 0.007 | 0.22 | 0.66 |
| v4-flash peak | 0.014 | 0.44 | 1.32 |

Peak is 01:00–04:00 and 06:00–10:00 UTC, weekdays only; everything else is off-peak at exactly half. Against the current `deepseek-v4-pro` row, and weighting by a real coding-agent token mix (95.6% cache read / 4.1% miss / 0.3% output, from an [8.04B-token trace](https://gist.github.com/hungson175/91147b729afdf9fd691342359265731b)), the status bar reads **2.26× low off-peak and 4.53× low at peak**; v4-flash is 1.91× / 3.82× low. The cache-hit rate alone moved 6.07× for pro, and in agent traffic that term is nine-tenths of the bill.

This one also interacts with #1: the `deepseek` heuristic falls back to `deepseek-chat` (`0.14 / 0.28`), so an unrecognised `deepseek-v4-pro-0813` gets Flash's old promo rate — roughly an order of magnitude off.

`cost()` takes no timestamp, so if you would rather not thread one through, storing the **peak** rate keeps the status bar an upper bound rather than a lower one. (Edge case if you ever re-price old sessions: whole-weekend off-peak only started 2026-08-23; before that weekends followed the weekday windows.)

## Minor

The Gemini section comment says `cacheRead = 10% of input`, but `gemini-2.0-flash` (0.025 on 0.1) and `gemini-2.0-flash-lite` (0.019 on 0.075) are at 25%. I believe the numbers are right for the 2.0 family and the comment simply predates them — worth a word so the next refresh does not "fix" the rows to match the comment.

---

Everything above is from the vendor pages linked inline. If a machine-readable cross-check helps, we keep a daily-refreshed 60-model dump with a `cached_input_per_million` column at [xyzs996/llm-api-pricing](https://github.com/xyzs996/llm-api-pricing) (JSON/CSV, CC-BY), and the DeepSeek time-of-day rule factored out with tests at [deepseek-peak-hours](https://github.com/xyzs996/deepseek-peak-hours).

title: Installer's CPU detection picks the wrong build on Ivy Bridge (AVX but no AVX2/FMA/BMI) → `Illegal instruction` at launch
body:
## Summary

The web installer (`curl -fsSL https://empryo.com/install.sh | bash`) auto-selects the standard `linux-x64` build on Intel Ivy Bridge CPUs (e.g. Xeon E5-2620 v2) because `/proc/cpuinfo` contains `avx`, but the shipped binary requires newer instructions (`avx2`, `fma`, `bmi1`, `bmi2`, `lzcnt`) that these CPUs lack. The install itself succeeds, but the installed binary dies immediately with `SIGILL` / `Illegal instruction (core dumped)`. The `x64-baseline` build works fine — it just never gets selected.

## Environment

- OS: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS (glibc 2.39)
- CPU: Intel(R) Xeon(R) E5-2620 v2 @ 2.10GHz (Ivy Bridge, 2013)
- Architecture: x86_64
- Install command: `curl -fsSL https://empryo.com/install.sh | bash`
- Version attempted: `3.6.3-beta` (latest at the time)
- Relevant CPU flags present: `sse2 ssse3 sse4_1 sse4_2 popcnt aes avx`
- Relevant CPU flags **missing**: `avx2 fma bmi1 bmi2 lzcnt avx512f`

## Steps to reproduce

1. On a machine with an Ivy Bridge (or older) x86_64 CPU, run:
   ```bash
   curl -fsSL https://empryo.com/install.sh | bash
   ```
2. Observe the installer: platform detection prints `linux-x64` (it does **not** fall back to `x64-baseline`), download/signature/checksum all pass, files extract to `~/.empryo/`, but the final runtime check fails:
   ```
   ERROR: installed binary failed to run:
   ```
3. Run the installed binary directly:
   ```bash
   ~/.empryo/bin/empryo --version
   ```
   Result:
   ```
   Illegal instruction (core dumped)
   ```
   Exit code 132 (SIGILL).

## Expected behavior

On a CPU that supports `avx` but not `avx2`/`fma`/`bmi`, the installer should either:
- auto-select the `x64-baseline` build, or
- print a clear message instructing the user to use the baseline build — before downloading anything.

Instead, the current heuristic wrongly considers the machine "supported" and only fails at the very end with an empty error message, which is very hard to diagnose.

## Root cause

In `install.sh`, the baseline fallback is gated on `avx` alone:

```bash
# Pre-Sandy Bridge x86_64 CPUs lack AVX; Bun's standard build SIGILLs there.
if [[ "$PLATFORM" == "linux" && "$ARCH" == "x64" ]]; then
  if ! grep -q avx /proc/cpuinfo 2>/dev/null; then
    note "cpu" "no AVX — selecting the baseline build"
    ARCH="x64-baseline"
  fi
fi
```

`avx` is present on **all** CPUs since Sandy Bridge (2011), including Ivy Bridge and Haswell. But the standard build is compiled for a much newer baseline: disassembling the binary shows `avx2`, `fma`, `bmi1/bmi2` and `lzcnt` instructions, all of which were introduced later (Haswell, 2013). The 143 MB standard binary crashes with `SIGILL` on the first such instruction. The detection predicate is simply too weak for the actual instruction-set requirements of the artifact it gates.

## Verification

Manually downloading `empryo-3.6.3-beta-linux-x64-baseline.tar.gz` (signature and sha-256 verified against the installer's pinned key) and running its bundled `install.sh` produces a fully working install:

```
$ ~/.empryo/bin/empryo --version
empryo 3.6.3-beta
```

So the baseline build itself is fine — only the auto-selection logic is broken.

## Suggested fix

Tighten the baseline check to match what the standard binary actually requires, e.g.:

```bash
# x64 standard build requires AVX2/FMA/BMI1/BMI2/LZCNT (Haswell+).
# Ivy Bridge and older (AVX but no AVX2) need the baseline build.
if [[ "$PLATFORM" == "linux" && "$ARCH" == "x64" ]]; then
  if ! grep -qE '\b(avx2|fma|bmi1|lzcnt)\b' /proc/cpuinfo 2>/dev/null; then
    note "cpu" "CPU lacks AVX2/FMA/BMI — selecting the baseline build"
    ARCH="x64-baseline"
  fi
fi
```

Also consider:
- Running the same check after install as a runtime sanity test, and if the binary dies with SIGILL, automatically re-installing the baseline build instead of failing with an empty message.
- Surfacing the actual failure (`Illegal instruction`) in the `ERROR: installed binary failed to run:` output — an empty message gives the user nothing to google.

## Workaround (until fixed)

Pin the baseline build explicitly:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://empryo.com/install.sh | EMPRYO_ARCH=x64-baseline bash
```

or manually download `empryo-<version>-linux-x64-baseline.tar.gz` from `https://dl.empryo.com/v<version>/` and run its bundled `install.sh`.

## Impact

This affects a broad class of older-but-common hardware: all Ivy Bridge and Sandy Bridge desktop/mobile CPUs, plus a large installed base of virtualized servers (any hypervisor exposing a pre-Haswell vCPU model, e.g. AWS `m3`/`c3`, older VMware/QEMU/KVM defaults). Those machines can never install Empryo via the standard command, and the failure mode (silent SIGILL with an empty error) makes it look like a broken install rather than a fixable detection issue.

Resize the terminal until the paragraph wraps.

## Actual behavior

Lines break at terminal-cell/character boundaries, including positions inside Thai words. Some combining-mark sequences can also make visual cursor placement look uneven depending on the terminal font.

## Expected behavior

Prose should use Unicode line-break opportunities and Thai word boundaries. Code blocks, paths, command output, and other preformatted content must retain character/cell wrapping.

## Evidence

The sample `ภาษาไทยทดสอบการตัดคำและการขึ้นบรรทัดใหม่` contains:

- 40 Unicode code points
- 34 grapheme clusters
- 11 Thai words according to `Intl.Segmenter('th', { granularity: 'word' })`

Current `src/components/chat/Markdown.tsx` delegates prose rendering to OpenTUI markdown. Table wrapping explicitly uses `wrapMode: "word"`, but whitespace-based word wrapping does not provide Thai dictionary boundaries because Thai normally omits spaces between words.

## Suggested implementation

- Segment prose using Unicode-aware word boundaries (`Intl.Segmenter`, locale auto-detection or `th`) and width using grapheme clusters.
- Expose or implement Unicode line breaking in OpenTUI's markdown/text wrapper rather than inserting visible spaces.
- Preserve code fences, inline code, URLs, paths, diffs, and raw tool output unchanged.
- Add tests covering Thai, combining marks, emoji ZWJ sequences, CJK, and Latin text.

OpenAlice should not rewrite the PTY stream downstream because that would corrupt ANSI cursor positioning; the fix needs to happen before Empryo lays out the TUI.

title: CommandCode Proxy Configuration Issue
body:
# CommandCode Proxy Configuration Issue

## Summary

Troubleshooting session for setting up a custom proxy server (CommandCode Go via local proxy) in empryo's `config.json`.

## Issues Encountered

### 1. Incorrect Provider Config Format

**Problem:** Initially converted empryo's `providers` array format to OpenCode's object format, which broke empryo's provider discovery.

**Wrong format (OpenCode style — breaks empryo):**
```json
"providers": {
  "commandcode": {
    "name": "CommandCode Go (via local proxy)",
    "package": "@opencode-ai/ai/providers/openai-compatible",
    "settings": {
      "baseURL": "http://127.0.0.1:18731/v1"
    },
    "models": { ... }
  }
}
```

**Correct format (empryo style):**
```json
"providers": [
  {
    "id": "commandcode",
    "name": "CommandCode Go (via local proxy)",
    "baseURL": "http://127.0.0.1:18731/v1",
    "envVar": "COMMANDCODE_API_KEY",
    "models": [
      "deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash",
      "meituan/LongCat-2.0:free",
      "zai-org/glm-5.3-flash",
      "meta/muse-spark-1.3-contributor",
      "meta/muse-spark-1.2-contributor"
    ]
  }
]
```

**Symptom:** After the wrong format was applied, `empryo --list-providers` no longer showed `commandcode`, and `/models` couldn't list the custom models.

**Fix:** Reverted to the array format. Provider reappeared immediately.

### 2. Unable to Add Key via TUI

**Problem:** empryo's TUI didn't provide a way to set the API key for the custom provider.

**Workaround:** Use the CLI command:
```bash
empryo --set-key commandcode YOUR_API_KEY
```

Or set the environment variable directly:
```bash
export COMMANDCODE_API_KEY=your_key_here
```


## Environment

- **Tool:** empryo (Go binary, ELF 64-bit)
- **Config location:** `/home/vagabond/.empryo/config.json`
- **Proxy:** CommandCode Go via local proxy at `http://127.0.0.1:18731/v1`
- **Env var:** `COMMANDCODE_API_KEY`
- **Models configured:** 5 models (DeepSeek V4 Flash, LongCat-2.0:Free, GLM-5.3-Flash, Muse Spark 1.3 Contributor, Muse Spark 1.2 Contributor)

## Easy-Migration Script

To prevent future mishaps, here's a quick reference for converting OpenCode's `opencode.json` to empryo's `config.json`:

### Key Differences

| Feature | OpenCode | empryo |
|---------|----------|--------|
| `providers` format | Object `{ "id": {...} }` | Array `[{ "id": ..., "baseURL": ..., "envVar": ... }]` |
| Model definition | Object `{ "model/model": { "modelID": ..., "variants": [...] } }` | Array of model ID strings `["model1", "model2"]` |
| Base URL | Inside `settings.baseURL` | Direct `baseURL` field |
| Env var | Inside `settings.env` array | Direct `envVar` field |
| Package | Required `package` field | Not used in empryo |

### Quick Conversion Rules

1. **OpenCode object → empryo array:**
   - Each key in `providers` object becomes an entry with `"id": "<key>"`
   - Move `settings.baseURL` → `baseURL` at top level
   - Move `settings.env[0]` → `envVar` at top level
   - Convert `models` object to array of model IDs (just the keys)

2. **Variants are lost:** empryo doesn't support OpenCode's `variants` concept natively — models are just IDs. If you need variants, you may need empyro's CLI flags (`--effort`, `--thinking`, etc.) at runtime.

3. **Other fields:** empryo ignores `package`, `settings`, `name` (display name) is preserved but not the `modelID`/`variants` structure.

### Example Migration

**OpenCode (`opencode.json`):**
```json
{
  "providers": {
    "commandcode": {
      "name": "CommandCode Go (via local proxy)",
      "package": "@opencode-ai/ai/providers/openai-compatible",
      "settings": { "baseURL": "http://127.0.0.1:18731/v1" },
      "models": {
        "deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash": {
          "modelID": "deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash",
          "name": "DeepSeek V4 Flash",
          "variants": [{ "id": "low", "settings": { "reasoningEffort": "low" } }]
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

**empryo (`config.json`):**
```json
{
  "providers": [
    {
      "id": "commandcode",
      "name": "CommandCode Go (via local proxy)",
      "baseURL": "http://127.0.0.1:18731/v1",
      "envVar": "COMMANDCODE_API_KEY",
      "models": ["deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash"]
    }
  ]
}
```

### One-Liner (jq)

To extract model IDs from an OpenCode config:
```bash
jq -r '.providers.commandcode.models | keys[]' ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json
```

To check your empryo providers:
```bash
empryo --list-providers
empryo --list-models commandcode
```

## Lessons Learned

1. empryo and OpenCode have **different config formats** — don't mix them up
2. empryo uses array format for `providers`, OpenCode uses object format
3. empryo's TUI may not support all operations — fall back to CLI flags
4. Always verify with `empryo --list-providers` after editing `config.json`

title: OrcaRouter provider support for Empryo
body:
Empryo is an AI coding agent that edits symbols, not strings: it parses a repository into a live graph on launch, so "what breaks if I touch this?" is answered before the first keystroke, and edits land as atomic, typecheck-gated AST operations in 30+ languages. Grep-and-patch agents never see those dependencies; Empryo does, which is what keeps its edits safe and its token bills small.

Its users treat model choice as a knob: Empryo routes ten task roles to any model from any of its 22 providers, per tab or per config, including any OpenAI-compatible endpoint. I'm an engineer on the OrcaRouter team, and I'd like to propose OrcaRouter as an optional provider so those users can reach many chat and reasoning models through one endpoint and one key.

## Proposal

I'm proposing [OrcaRouter](https://www.orcarouter.ai) as an additional, **optional** provider for Empryo. It would not replace or change any existing provider, key, default, or routing behavior. OrcaRouter exposes an OpenAI-compatible API and uses standard API-key authentication, so the natural integration point is a new provider entry in `src/core/llm/providers/` alongside the existing OpenAI-compatible backends, following the `ProviderDefinition` interface you already use. Nothing here is implemented yet — this is a proposal to see whether it's worth pursuing.

A few OrcaRouter capabilities that map onto how Empryo already works:

- **Multiple models through one endpoint.** A single API key provides access to many chat and reasoning models, which fits Empryo's "one agent, many brains" pattern of mixing models inside a single run.
- **Automatic model routing and provider failover.** When an upstream provider is erroring or rate-limited, OrcaRouter can route to a fallback — the same high-availability concern raised in the model-fallback discussion on this tracker.
- **Prompt caching.** Routed requests reuse cache prefixes, which complements Empryo's cache-aware routing and keeps long sessions cheap.
- **Usage tracking and budgets.** Itemized spend per model supports Empryo's per-model, per-tab cost tracking, and team budget controls matter for shared workspaces.

## Ecosystem

OrcaRouter is already integrated by open-source projects such as [RAGFlow](https://github.com/infiniflow/ragflow), [Dify](https://github.com/langgenius/dify), [goose](https://github.com/block/goose), and [promptfoo](https://github.com/promptfoo/promptfoo), all through the same OpenAI-compatible surface. More examples are listed at https://www.orcarouter.ai/built-with.

## Disclosure

OrcaRouter runs an optional open-source partner program: approved OSS projects can receive a 5% revenue share from OrcaRouter usage attributed to their integration. Participation is not a prerequisite for the integration, and I'm happy to follow Empryo's disclosure and governance expectations however you'd like to handle it.

If this sounds useful, I'd welcome your thoughts — and with your go-ahead I'd be glad to submit an implementation PR following CONTRIBUTING.md, where LLM provider additions are already in scope.

title: diagnostics reports phantom JSX parse errors on any file containing JSX (.tsx and .ts) — the TS server is opened with languageId "typescript", and swapping/ disabling LSP servers does not change it
body:
## Summary `analyze` with `action: "diagnostics"` reports dozens of bogus TypeScript parse errors on every `.tsx` file. The code is valid; Empryo's LSP layer opens `.tsx` documents with `languageId: "typescript"` instead of `"typescriptreact"`, so the TypeScript server parses JSX as a comparison operator plus a regex literal and cascades ~26 errors per JSX tag. `.ts` files are unaffected, which is what makes this easy to misread as real breakage. ## Environment - Empryo `3.8.1-beta` (ProductVersion `3.8.1.0`) - Windows 11 x64, desktop app - Project: Vite + React 19 + TypeScript 7.0.2, `tsconfig.json` has `"jsx": "react-jsx"` - LSP servers installed: `typescript-language-server` 6.0.0, `biome` 2.5.11, and others ## Reproduction 1. Open any React + TypeScript project. 2. Run `analyze` with `action: "diagnostics"` on a `.tsx` file. Minimal repro file `src/__probe_jsx.tsx`: ```tsx export function Probe() { return
hi
; } ``` Result: **12 diagnostics, 11 errors** — every one of them fake. ``` error src/__probe_jsx.tsx:2:14 [parse] — expected `>` but instead found `className` error src/__probe_jsx.tsx:2:9 [parse] — Invalid assignment to `
' expected. error src/__probe_jsx.tsx:2:23 [1005] — ';' expected. error src/__probe_jsx.tsx:2:31 [1161] — Unterminated regular expression literal. error src/__probe_jsx.tsx:2:10 [2304] — Cannot find name 'div'. error src/__probe_jsx.tsx:2:14 [2304] — Cannot find name 'className'. error src/__probe_jsx.tsx:2:24 [2365] — Operator '<' cannot be applied to types 'boolean' and 'RegExp'. error src/__probe_jsx.tsx:2:28 [2304] — Cannot find name 'hi'. hint src/__probe_jsx.tsx:2:24 [7027] — Unreachable code detected. ``` The `2304 Cannot find name 'div'` and `2365 Operator '<' cannot be applied to types 'boolean' and 'RegExp'` are the signature of JSX being tokenized as `(<)(div)(className)(>)(hi)()`. ## Root cause — proven in isolation I launched `typescript-language-server` (the same 6.0.0 binary Empryo uses) directly against that exact file over stdio and sent `textDocument/didOpen` twice, changing only `languageId`: | `languageId` | Diagnostics | | --- | --- | | `typescriptreact` | **0** | | `typescript` | **8** — `1005 '>' expected`, `1005 ';' expected`, `1161 Unterminated regular expression literal`, `2304 Cannot find name 'div'`, `2304 Cannot find name 'className'`, … | Byte-identical file, identical server, identical workspace — the `languageId` is the entire difference. `textDocument/languageId` drives `ScriptKind` in the TypeScript server, and only `typescriptreact` / `javascriptreact` enable JSX parsing. `tsconfig`'s `"jsx": "react-jsx"` does not rescue it, because the LSP server never parses the document as JSX in the first place. The extension mapping does exist somewhere in the bundle — `typescriptreact` appears 62 times and `javascriptreact` 32 times inside `resources/app.asar` — so this is a wiring bug in the path that picks the `languageId` for a `.tsx` / `.jsx` document, not a missing constant. ## Scope Failure correlates with the file extension, not with content or with the project: | File | Result | | --- | --- | | `src/App.tsx` | 116 diagnostics (89 error, 23 warning) — all `[parse]` | | `src/components/Projects.tsx` | 39 diagnostics (27 error) — all `[parse]` | | `src/i18n.tsx` | 11 diagnostics (8 error) — all `[parse]` | | `.tsx` file with no JSX in it | No diagnostics — clean | | `src/content.ts` (plain `.ts`, same project) | No diagnostics — clean | So the real signal is not merely drowned, it is inverted: the worst-looking files are the ones that are fine, and a `.tsx` file with a genuine type error is indistinguishable from one that parses. ## Secondary issue — results are non-deterministic across identical calls Three consecutive calls to `analyze(action: "diagnostics", file: "src/App.tsx")` in the same session returned three different answers for the same unchanged file: 1. `No diagnostics — file is clean` 2. `54 diagnostic(s): 37 error(s), 15 warning(s)` 3. `117 diagnostic(s): 89 error(s), 23 warning(s)` Collapsing the diagnostics to "clean" on one of those calls means a first run can hide a real error set. This looks like a cached result being returned before (or instead of) the LSP response — the counts differing between calls 2 and 3 also suggests partial buffers being reported as complete. ## Secondary issue — `codeIntelligence.backend` has no effect on this path Per the docs, [code intelligence is layered](https://empryo.com/docs/concepts/intelligence) and falls through LSP → ts-morph → tree-sitter → regex. For diagnostics, the configured backend appears to be ignored: - `codeIntelligence.backend = "ts-morph"` → identical diagnostics - `codeIntelligence.backend = "tree-sitter"` → identical diagnostics - `codeIntelligence.backend = "auto"` → identical diagnostics I set and reverted the key via the `settings` tool each time, and the output was the same to the character. Either the setting never reaches the `diagnostics` action, or `diagnostics` is hard-wired to the LSP tier without attempting a fallback. That matters here specifically: ts-morph parses TSX correctly, so the documented fallback chain would have masked this bug entirely had it been tried. ## Expected behavior 1. `.tsx` documents open with `languageId: "typescriptreact"` and `.jsx` with `"javascriptreact"`. Every other extension keeps its current mapping. 2. If the LSP backend returns parse-level errors for a file it was handed with the wrong language mode, or fails outright, the documented fallback to ts-morph / tree-sitter fires rather than surfacing the raw parser output to the model. 3. A diagnostics result is either the complete set from one backend or an honest error — not a truncated or empty set that later reads as "clean". ## Suggested tests - A `.tsx` fixture with JSX (self-closing tags, fragments, generics alongside JSX, `as` casts in props) asserting zero parse diagnostics. - An extension → `languageId` table test covering `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.mts`, `.cts`, `.js`, `.jsx`, `.mjs`, `.cjs`. - A regression test that a real type error in a `.tsx` file still surfaces (so the fix cannot be "swallow everything from JSX files"). - A determinism test: repeated `diagnostics` calls on an unchanged file return identical sets. ## Impact Diagnostics is the tool an agent uses to check its own edits, so on any React or Next.js codebase the signal is unusable — agents either chase 100+ phantom errors or, worse, get the "clean" answer above and conclude a broken file is fine. Worth noting because the model's own output is what gets reported back: in this session the diagnostics readout was almost reported as a real list of 89 errors in a file that compiles cleanly under `tsc --noEmit`. ## How I verified the files are actually clean ``` npx tsc --noEmit → passed npx biome check src/App.tsx → 0 diagnostics (matches the LSP exactly when it uses the right languageId) ```

title: Marionette fast lane silently degrades to index-only on custom OpenAI-compatible providers (schema never sent + xhigh reasoning burns the output budget)
body:
### Environment
- Empryo desktop 3.8.2-beta (also repros headless via the CLI binary), macOS arm64
- Model provider: custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint (Nous portal, `providers` block in config)
- Marionette: `agentFeatures.marionette: true`, `marionetteMode: "fast"`

### Symptom
Every marionette compile logs `fast failed → index only` and the map is the mechanical retrieval fallback ("Mechanically retrieved map — no model read this request"). `~/.empryo/marionette-usage.json` only ever records `lanes.none`. The degrade message is:

```
The fast lane's model call failed (No object generated: response did not match schema.) — this map is retrieval only.
```

Reproduced with four different model families on the same endpoint: `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash`, `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash`, `~openai/gpt-mini-latest`, `~anthropic/claude-haiku-latest` — so it is not model quality.

### Wire capture (local logging reverse-proxy as the provider)
Two stacked defects in the compile request (`POST /v1/chat/completions`):

1. **The output schema never reaches the model.** The request carries `response_format: {"type":"json_object"}` and the system prompt ends with "reply with a single json object matching the output schema — no prose, no markdown fence", but the schema itself appears nowhere in the request — not in `response_format` (no `json_schema`), not injected into the messages. The model cannot know the required shape (`asks`/`interpretation`/`focus`/`connections`/`memories`/`unknowns`). The gpt-mini reasoning trace captured on the wire says exactly this: *"there's no clear output schema given in the prompt, so I'll have to infer the necessary fields."*

2. **`reasoning_effort: "xhigh"` (from `performance.effort`) with `max_tokens: 8192`.** Reasoning models spend the entire output budget thinking and return `content: null`, `finish_reason: "length"` (`native_finish_reason: "max_output_tokens"`). With no content there is nothing to parse, so the salvage path and the repair pass (which re-sends with the same 8192 cap) can never recover.

Net effect: on any custom OpenAI-compatible provider, the fast/assist/deep lanes can never produce a map — the pre-pass silently degrades to `none` on every prompt while still paying for the failed call.

### Workaround (config-only, verified)
Dedicated single-model provider + `extraBody` override + `taskRouter.marionette`:

```json
{
  "extraBody": {
    "nous-fast": {
      "reasoning_effort": "none",
      "response_format": {
        "type": "json_schema",
        "json_schema": { "name": "marionette_map", "strict": true, "schema": { "...full map schema..." : "see zod schema in the marionette module" } }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

With the schema on the wire and reasoning off, the same compile that failed on four model families returns `finish_reason: "stop"`, `lane: fast`, in ~28s.

### Suggested fix
- For openai-compatible providers in `generateObject` mode, actually deliver the schema: send `response_format: {"type":"json_schema", ...}` when the endpoint supports it, else inject the JSON schema into the prompt.
- Clamp (or drop) reasoning effort for the pre-pass — a locator pass gains nothing from `xhigh`, and at the fixed 8192 output cap any reasoning model returns empty content.
- Consider scaling the compile's output cap with the model's declared `maxOutputTokens` instead of the fixed 8192.

Happy to share the full wire capture (redacted) if useful.
