title: Hooks do not inherit `HERDR_*` env vars — breaks Herdr's custom-agent recipe and can misreport state onto the wrong pane
body:
## Summary

Herdr's documented path for integrating an unsupported agent is:

> "An agent running in a Herdr pane inherits `HERDR_ENV`, `HERDR_PANE_ID`, `HERDR_BIN_PATH`, and `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`. If the agent exposes lifecycle hooks, use those hooks to report semantic state"
> — https://herdr.dev/docs/integrations/

Empryo exposes lifecycle hooks — but its hook subprocesses **do not inherit any `HERDR_*` variable**, so that recipe cannot work as written.

This matters for more than "the integration silently does nothing": because `HERDR_PANE_ID` is missing, `herdr pane ... --current` does not fail, it **resolves to the focused pane**. A hook written against the documented recipe therefore reports agent state onto whichever pane the user happens to be looking at, silently mislabeling an unrelated agent's row.

Context: issue #117 ("Feature request: SoulForge support in Herdr") was closed with the guidance to follow Herdr's custom-agent instructions. This is the blocker for exactly that path.

## Why it happens

Empryo builds the environment for hook subprocesses from an allowlist rather than passing `process.env`. The allowlist already covers terminal-integration variables for other multiplexers:

```
K5a = PATH HOME USER SHELL LANG TERM TERM_PROGRAM EDITOR VISUAL TMPDIR …
      KITTY_WINDOW_ID  WEZTERM_PANE  NVIM_APPNAME  OTUI_TREE_SITTER_WORKER_PATH …
H5a = LC_  XDG_  npm_config_  npm_lifecycle_  SSH_
```

`KITTY_WINDOW_ID` and `WEZTERM_PANE` are precisely this same class of variable — Herdr simply wasn't known when the list was written.

Note the filter itself is good and should stay: hooks are user-authored shell commands, and passing the full environment through would leak secrets such as the `INTEGRATES_API_TOKEN` that MCP servers are configured with. **The ask is a narrow addition, not the removal of the filter.**

## Reproduction

1. Inside a Herdr pane, temporarily add to `~/.empryo/hooks.json`:

```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "PreToolUse": [
      { "hooks": [ { "type": "command", "command": "env > /tmp/empryo-hook-env.txt", "async": false } ] }
    ]
  }
}
```

2. In that same pane, run Empryo (TUI or `--headless`) and trigger any tool call.
3. Inspect the dump:

```bash
grep -c '^HERDR_' /tmp/empryo-hook-env.txt
# expected: 6   (HERDR_ENV, HERDR_PANE_ID, HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID, HERDR_TAB_ID, HERDR_BIN_PATH, HERDR_SOCKET_PATH)
# actual:   0
```

The Empryo process itself does have them — only the hook subprocess loses them.

## The part that makes it dangerous

Measured in the same shell, same instant, inside a Herdr pane:

```bash
$ herdr pane current --current
  # -> cwd: .../groups/misc      (my pane)

$ env -u HERDR_ENV -u HERDR_PANE_ID -u HERDR_SOCKET_PATH -u HERDR_BIN_PATH \
      herdr pane current --current
  # -> cwd: .../groups/wanda     focused: true   <-- a different pane
```

This matches Herdr's own warning ("Omitting a target may use the UI-focused pane, which can belong to the user or another client"). So a hook that follows the documented recipe will report onto the focused pane instead of erroring out.

## Requested change

Add these to the hook environment allowlist:

```
HERDR_ENV
HERDR_PANE_ID
HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID
HERDR_TAB_ID
HERDR_BIN_PATH
HERDR_SOCKET_PATH
```

All six are non-secret identifiers/paths injected by Herdr into the pane, on the same footing as the `KITTY_WINDOW_ID` / `WEZTERM_PANE` entries already present.

Optional, if cheap: document the allowlist in https://empryo.com/docs/tools/hooks/ so integrators know which variables survive, and mention that hooks are sandboxed from the parent environment by design.

## Workaround (no change required from your side)

It is possible to make this work today with a launcher wrapper: capture `HERDR_PANE_ID` before Empryo starts, persist it keyed by the launcher's PID (`exec` keeps the PID), and have the hook resolve the pane by walking up its ancestor PIDs instead of reading the environment. That is what I'm running locally, and it works — but it requires launching Empryo through a wrapper rather than directly, which is a real cost for every user who wants Herdr integration, and it's why the allowlist addition would be the better fix.

## Environment

- Empryo `3.8.6-beta` (macOS 26.7, arm64)
- Herdr `0.8.2` (`herdr pane report-agent` / `report-agent-session` / `release-agent` all present and working)

title: Python imports produce no import-proven edges: tree-sitter outline stores raw statement text as source, and isResolvable excludes bare module names
body:
## Summary

Python import edges are broken in the primary RepoMap path, in two stacked ways. The visible symptom: `getFileDependents()` / blast-radius undercounts for Python modules — measured downstream as a module with 7 real importers reporting **0 dependents** — and nothing in the map output signals the gap.

## Defect 1 (primary): `getFileOutline()` never extracts a normalized Python import source

`RepoMap.indexFile` obtains imports via `this.treeSitter.getFileOutline(absPath)` (~line 786); there is no regex-backend fallback for imports on this path.

The main Python query (`backends/tree-sitter.ts` ~line 42) is:

```
(import_statement) @import
(import_from_statement) @import
```

— no `@source` capture (compare TypeScript: `(import_statement source: (string) @source) @import`). `getFileOutline` then falls back (~lines 856-870):

```ts
const source = sourceCapture ? sourceCapture.node.text.replace(/['"]/g, "") : node.text;
```

so every Python import is recorded with `source` = the **raw statement text**:

| statement        | recorded `imp.source`      | should be |
|------------------|----------------------------|-----------|
| `import foo`       | `"import foo"`               | `foo`       |
| `from foo import X`  | `"from foo import X"`        | `foo`       |
| `from pkg.m import X`| `"from pkg.m import X"`      | `pkg.m`     |
| `from .u import X`   | `"from .u import X"`         | `.u`        |

`resolveImportSource` receives these raw strings and fails on all of them (none match the expected shapes; the dotted branch turns `"from pkg.m import X"` into `"from pkg/m import X"` and `"from .u import X"` into `"from /u import X"` — still not a path that resolves). Note that `TreeSitterBackend.findImports` (~line 624) already has a better Python query — `(import_from_statement module_name: (dotted_name) @source) @import` — but RepoMap uses `getFileOutline`, not `findImports`. (That query still misses `from . import x`, since `module_name` is a `relative_import` node there, not `dotted_name`.)

A side effect worth noting: raw strings containing `.` (e.g. `"from pkg.m import X"`, `"from .u import X"`) pass `isResolvable`, so `import_source` gets populated with unresolvable raw text — poison rows that remain permanently unresolved and are repeatedly retried whenever `resolveUnresolvedRefs` runs.

## Defect 2 (latent): `isResolvable` excludes Python bare-module names even once sources are normalized

When sources are normalized, `import foo` produces `source = "foo"`, which fails every `isResolvable` check (`./`, `crate::`, `super::`, `\\`, dotted, Go prefix, tsconfig) → `import_source` stays NULL → no confidence-3 edge in `buildEdges` Phase 1a, and `resolveUnresolvedRefs` cannot retry it (its filter is `import_source IS NOT NULL`).

## Second-order gap

The bare-source fallback in `resolveImportSource` resolves repo-root-relative only (`lib/<src>`, `<src>` anchored to `this.cwd`). Script-style sibling imports — `hooks/b.py` doing `import a` against `hooks/a.py`, valid when `hooks/` is on `sys.path` (e.g. direct script execution, common in scripts/tests layouts) — produce `source_file_id = NULL`. This is context-dependent semantics, not universal, but the shape is common enough to cover.

## Fix requirements

- Normalize Python sources at extraction: extend the main query with `module_name: (dotted_name) @source` plus a `relative_import` capture for `from .x import y` (and dotted names for `import_statement`), matching `findImports` but covering the relative case it misses.
- Record the resolvable candidate independently of first-pass resolution success — i.e. store `import_source` when the *shape* is plausibly local (per language), not only when `resolveImportSource` returned non-null. Gating storage on successful resolution leaves `source_file_id = NULL, import_source = NULL` for late-indexed targets and keeps the retry pass permanently blind.
- Optionally: importer-relative fallback for bare Python sources.

## Minimal repro

```
a.py:  X = 1
b.py:  import a            # or: from a import X
```

After indexing, `refs` for `b.py` shows `source_file_id NULL` and `import_source` either NULL or raw statement text; `getFileDependents("a.py")` returns `[]`. Expected: confidence-3 import edge.

## Test gap

`tests/regex-backend.test.ts` ~149-154 covers `from os.path import join, exists` against `RegexBackend` only — nothing exercises Python through `getFileOutline`/`RepoMap`/`getFileDependents`. Suggested coverage: `import foo`, `from foo import X`, `from pkg.foo import X`, `from .foo import X` through the real path, asserting `import_source`, `source_file_id`, confidence 3, and `getFileDependents()` in both indexing orders (target-before-importer and importer-before-target).

title: YOLO setting does not persist on WSL
body:
$## Bug

The `yolo` setting cannot be persisted from the Empryo CLI on WSL.

### Environment

- Empryo: `3.8.6-beta`
- Surface: TUI / CLI
- OS: WSL (Linux)
- Config path: `~/.empryo/config.json`

### Reproduction

1. Enable YOLO mode in the CLI.
2. Persist it through the settings path with `yolo = true`, targeting either global or project scope.
3. Restart or query the setting again.

### Actual behavior

The settings operation reports:

```text
yolo: (unset) → (unset) (global) — unchanged
```

The same happens for project scope. `settings.get("yolo")` continues to report `unset`, and `~/.empryo/config.json` contains no `yolo` entry. Passing the value as either a boolean or the string `"true"` produces the same result.

The live UI reports that the change was applied, but no persistent value is written.

### Expected behavior

Persisting `yolo: true` should write the setting to the selected config scope and `settings.get("yolo")` should return `true` after reopening the CLI.

This appears to be a persistence/serialization issue specific to the `yolo` boolean setting, rather than a permissions or path issue.

title: Windows Desktop model picker updates UI/default model but active tab remains on previous model
body:
## Environment

- **Platform:** Windows Desktop
- **Empryo:** 3.8.6-beta
- **Project path:** contains non-ASCII/Cyrillic characters — noted for context, but the model-switch defect below is separate from the already-fixed external hook encoding issue.

## User-visible symptom

Switching the active model in Desktop with the normal model picker updates the header/UI, but the active tab/session keeps running on the previous model.

Example:

- previous model: `subscriptions/gpt-5.6-luna`
- selected model: `openrouter/z-ai/glm-5.3-flash`

The Desktop header immediately shows `openrouter/z-ai/glm-5.3-flash`, while the active tab/session continues to report and use `subscriptions/gpt-5.6-luna`.

## Reproduction

1. Start a Desktop session using `subscriptions/gpt-5.6-luna`.
2. In the same active tab, use the normal model picker / Ctrl+L.
3. Select `openrouter/z-ai/glm-5.3-flash`.
4. Observe that the Desktop header changes to GLM.
5. Send another prompt in the **same** tab.
6. Inspect persisted session metadata:
   `<cwd>\.empryo\sessions\<session>\meta.json`
   Resolve `activeTabId` → matching `tabs[].activeModel`.

Observed:

```
SESSION_MODEL: subscriptions/gpt-5.6-luna
```

while the Desktop header displays `openrouter/z-ai/glm-5.3-flash`.

## Concrete evidence

- Observed active tab: `ACTIVE_TAB_ID: t_muar8zen_1`
- Persisted runtime model: `SESSION_MODEL: subscriptions/gpt-5.6-luna`
- At the same time the Desktop header visibly displayed `openrouter/z-ai/glm-5.3-flash`

A PreToolUse diagnostic reading the session-tab runtime state during the next dispatch also observed:

```
BLOCK tool=Agent
model=subscriptions/gpt-5.6-luna
source=session-tab
```

This confirms the stale session model was not merely an old file inspected later — it was the runtime-visible active tab model at the next tool call.

## Expected

When selecting a model in the normal Desktop model picker:

1. header/UI selected model changes;
2. current active chat/tab model changes;
3. next turn uses the selected model;
4. persisted `TabMeta.activeModel` reflects the selected model.

All four should agree immediately. Expected after selecting GLM:

- UI: `openrouter/z-ai/glm-5.3-flash`
- current active chat: `openrouter/z-ai/glm-5.3-flash`
- session meta `tabs[activeTabId].activeModel`: `openrouter/z-ai/glm-5.3-flash`
- next turn: GLM

## Actual

- UI/header: GLM
- active tab/session runtime: previous Luna model

Therefore: **DISPLAYED MODEL ≠ ACTIVE TAB MODEL**

## Likely defect boundary

Current upstream source appears to intentionally update both states during model selection:

```js
activeChatRef.current?.setActiveModel(modelId)
setActiveModelForHeader(modelId)
saveToScope({ defaultModel: modelId }, ...)
```

The installed 3.8.6-beta Desktop behavior does not satisfy that invariant.

Please investigate the Desktop model-selection lifecycle around:

- header model state;
- `activeChatRef` / `chat.setActiveModel`;
- per-tab `activeModel`;
- model picker callback;
- session persistence;
- next-turn model resolution.

Do not assume the defect is only persistence. The important invariant is:

```
SELECTED MODEL = HEADER MODEL = ACTIVE CHAT MODEL = NEXT TURN MODEL = PERSISTED TAB MODEL
```

## Impact

Misleading and potentially expensive: the UI can show one provider/model while subsequent work continues on another. It also breaks external supported integrations that correctly inspect the active tab model from session state.

## Acceptance

A fix should pass this exact same-session sequence with no restart:

- Luna → Ctrl+L → GLM → next turn is GLM → active tab metadata is GLM
- GLM → Ctrl+L → Luna → next turn is Luna → active tab metadata is Luna

Header, runtime and persisted `activeModel` must remain consistent.

## Attachment

Evidence screenshot exists (header = `OpenRouter/z-ai/glm-5.3-flash`, gate/session evidence = `subscriptions/gpt-5.6-luna`); the CLI/API path used to file this issue cannot upload image attachments, so the key observed values are quoted verbatim in the Evidence section above. The screenshot can be added to this issue on request.

(No secrets or unrelated project contents included.)

body:
**Setup:** one TUI session acts as an orchestrator. It starts long-running work with `background_dispatch` (up to 4 agents at a time, no `resident`) and with background shell jobs, then ends its turn and waits to be resumed. `agentFeatures.backgroundAutoResume` is `true`.

**Problem:** the orchestrator often stays idle after the background work finishes. It waits until I type something.

1. **Background shell jobs:** when a background shell (for example a long `python ... watch` command) exits, the parent is not resumed. The job file under `<cwd>/.empryo/jobs/job-N.json` ends with `"status":"done","reported":false`. This happened for every one of ~6 shell jobs today.
2. **Background agents:** as a workaround, I moved the wait into a background agent, since an agent finishing should resume the parent. This works most of the time, but around 1 in 4 times the agent shows "Background agent finished" in the transcript and the parent stays idle. It happens most when several agents finish close together, or when an agent finishes while the parent is ending its own turn.

**Expected:** every finished background agent or shell job resumes an idle parent, or queues a wake-up that fires when the current turn ends. A completion should never be dropped.

**Impact:** a multi-agent run stalls for 10–30 minutes each time, until someone types into the session. Right now I use an external script that types a "resume" message into the terminal when the session looks idle.

**Related behavior (maybe worth documenting):**
- At most 4 resident agents; a 5th `resident: true` silently runs as non-resident.
- A resident conversation closes after 12 exchanges.
- A round that ends with an empty or text-only final message is reported as "No output from agent" and removes the resident.

- 10:49:29 PM: 10% → 10%, 12 → 4 messages, 1,080-char summary. Its Task was the first message sent after 10:44 ("go ahead and squash merge this into main…"), and it listed only the two `gh` commands, with no files from the earlier work.

### Impact

Each compaction keeps only the work since the previous compaction. In long sessions, or whenever compaction runs often, the agent loses the original task and earlier decisions after the second compaction.

title: macOS: startup crashes when creating the memory trigram index
body:
## Description

Empryo fails to start with:

```text
SQLiteError: error in tokenizer constructor
    at ensureTrigramTable (/$bunfs/root/empryo:1092:19)
```

### Environment

- Empryo: `3.9.0-beta`
- Bun: `1.4.2`
- Platform: macOS, Darwin `24.6.0`, arm64
- Runtime SQLite: `3.43.2`

### Steps to reproduce

1. Launch `empryo`.
2. Startup fails during memory initialization.

### Cause

`ensureTrigramTable()` creates an FTS5 index with:

```sql
tokenize="trigram case_sensitive 0 remove_diacritics 1"
```

SQLite `3.43.2` rejects the `remove_diacritics` option for the trigram tokenizer.

Isolated tests in a fresh in-memory database confirm:

- SQLite `3.43.2`, original options: fails with the same error.
- SQLite `3.43.2`, without `remove_diacritics 1`: succeeds.
- SQLite `3.53.4`, original options: succeeds.

Both existing memory databases pass `PRAGMA quick_check`, so this does not appear to be database corruption.

### Expected behavior

Empryo starts successfully with a compatible SQLite library or supported tokenizer options.

### Suggested fix

Either load a compatible SQLite library before opening databases, or detect tokenizer support and fall back to compatible options.

Also include memory-index initialization in `empryo doctor`. Currently, all eight checks pass despite this startup failure.

title: Desktop bridge: unhandledRejection "JSON.stringify cannot serialize BigInt" during multi-agent run
body:
## Summary

While one agent was running with 3 subagents in the desktop app, a toast appeared:

> Background error (unhandledRejection) ×3
> TypeError: JSON.stringify cannot serialize BigInt.

The agents kept running and nothing was visibly lost, but a `BigInt` reaches a `JSON.stringify` call inside the desktop bridge. The call throws inside a promise with no `.catch`, so it surfaces as an unhandled rejection.

## Environment

- Empryo 3.9.0-beta, desktop app (log surface: `desktop-bridge`)
- Linux 6.18 (WSL2), x86_64
- Workload: 1 main agent + 3 background subagents (`bg-1`..`bg-3`), editing a TS/React monorepo in parallel
- The user's project has no `BigInt` usage in its own TS/TSX/MJS sources, so the value comes from Empryo itself or one of its servers/providers.

## Evidence

`~/.empryo/logs/errors.jsonl` has two entries, with no stack trace:

```json
{"ts":"2026-10-04T07:40:34.014Z","pid":14105,"surface":"desktop-bridge","source":"unhandledRejection","message":"TypeError: JSON.stringify cannot serialize BigInt."}
{"ts":"2026-10-05T19:14:39.986Z","pid":2876,"surface":"desktop-bridge","source":"unhandledRejection","message":"TypeError: JSON.stringify cannot serialize BigInt."}
```

Entries logged just before each one (same process):

- 2026-10-05 19:13:59: `resource-guard memory 1589MB over the 1536MB ceiling (plus 3271MB in spawned servers) — declining type-aware analysis`
- 2026-10-05 19:14:33 and 19:14:35: `LSP textDocument/diagnostic failed ...` followed by `LSP diagnostics failed for ...` (vscode-eslint-language-server, via mason)
- 2026-10-04 07:21 to 07:23: the same LSP diagnostics failure pair on other files
- Right after the 2026-10-04 entry: `LSP:.../typescript-language-server killed by SIGTERM`

I did not verify the LSP failures cause the error. They are the only repeated activity before both events, so they are a lead, not a diagnosis.

## Expected behavior

No unhandled rejection. A `BigInt` in a payload should be serialized (for example as a string) or dropped, and the failure should be caught and logged with context.

## Why it is hard to debug today

The unhandled-rejection handler records only `message`. There is no stack, no originating call site, and no payload type. The same message cannot be traced to a feature.

## Suggested fix

1. Find the `JSON.stringify` call(s) in the desktop bridge that serialize agent, subagent, LSP or tool-result state. Add a shared safe serializer:
   ```ts
   const safeStringify = (v: unknown) =>
     JSON.stringify(v, (_k, x) => (typeof x === 'bigint' ? x.toString() : x));
   ```
   Use it for bridge, event and IPC payloads.
2. Add a `.catch` on the async path so a serialization failure is logged with the event type, not raised as an unhandled rejection.
3. Include `error.stack` in the `unhandledRejection` log entry in `errors.jsonl`.
4. Add a regression test: a payload that contains a `BigInt` (for example in a tool result or LSP diagnostic) must not throw.

## Impact

Low to medium. The toast is noisy (×3) and some UI or state sync update is probably dropped. The agents continued to run.

title: Skills: ~/.claude/skills copy shadows a same-named ~/.empryo/skills copy
body:
## What happens

When the same skill name exists in `~/.empryo/skills/` and `~/.claude/skills/`, Empryo loads the `~/.claude/skills/` copy. Empryo's own folder loses to Claude Code's.

That makes it impossible to keep an Empryo-adapted copy of a skill next to a Claude Code copy of the same name. Anyone who uses both tools and keeps adapted copies hits this: the Empryo copy never loads.

## Expected

`~/.empryo/skills/` wins over `~/.claude/skills/` (and `~/.agents/skills/`) on a name clash. Or a setting that lists which skill folders Empryo reads, so a user can drop `~/.claude/skills/`.

## Repro (Empryo 3.9.1-beta, macOS)

What we ran: two different `SKILL.md` files under the same skill name, one in each folder. In an empty folder:

```
empryo --headless --events --mode plan "Call the skills tool to load the skill named <name>. Then quote verbatim the line in the loaded text that starts with '<a line only one copy has>'."
```

The `skills` tool's `load` result carried the `~/.claude/skills/` text, and the answer quoted the `~/.claude/skills/` copy's line. The prompt named neither copy's wording, so the model could not echo it.

A minimal version (not run as written): put `MARKER: empryo copy` in `~/.empryo/skills/demo/SKILL.md` and `MARKER: claude copy` in `~/.claude/skills/demo/SKILL.md`, then ask the `skills` tool to load `demo`.

From reading the code (below), `--skill <name>`, `skills.autoLoad` and session restore go through the same catalog, so they should resolve the same way. We did not run those three.

## Where it comes from (bundled JS, 3.9.1-beta)

- The scan-root list lists, in order: `~/.empryo/skills`, the second Empryo dot dir, `~/.agents/skills`, `~/.claude/skills`, then the project roots (`<project>/.empryo/skills`, `<project>/.agents/skills`, `<project>/.claude/skills`).
- The catalog builder walks those roots in order and does `map.set(name, entry)` for each skill. It dedupes by real path only, so a later root overwrites an earlier one with the same name: **last folder wins**.
- The catalog feeds the `skills` tool, `--skill`, `skills.autoLoad` and session restore.
- The single-name lookup used after a skills.sh install walks the same roots and **returns the first match**, so `~/.empryo/skills` wins there. The two paths disagree.

Project roots winning over global ones looks intended. Among the global roots, Empryo's own folder losing to Claude Code's looks unintended.

## Suggested fix

Either of:

1. Make the catalog first-wins among global roots (as the single-name lookup already is), keeping project roots above global ones.
2. Add a setting such as `skills.folders` (or `skills.scanClaude: false`) listing the folders Empryo reads.

Also useful: the `skills` tool's `list` result could include each skill's resolved path. Today it returns scope and text only, so a user can't see which copy won.

title: Genome watcher indexes ~/Library churn when opened in the home directory, breaking prompt cache every turn
body:
**Version:** 3.9.4-beta (latest), macOS arm64, desktop app

## What happens
If you open Empryo on the home directory (`~`), the prompt cache breaks and every turn gets flooded with Genome deltas.

1. The first Genome scan sees the home folder and indexes nothing, as designed: `Opened in home directory or system root — no files indexed`. The first turn's system prompt says "Code intelligence limited: No symbols indexed".
2. The file watcher keeps running, though. It indexes every file that changes under `~/Library` (browser caches, app databases, Spotlight metadata, `.plist` files). These files change all the time.
3. At the start of the next turn, the Genome map is admitted and the system prompt changes from "No symbols indexed" to a map of `Library/...` files. Result: `Cache broke · system prompt changed (block 3/3 text, +2087 chars)`. The `meanwhile` list shows `genome map re-rendered (admitted at turn start) → epoch 1`.
4. Every turn after that comes with a `<genome_update>` block of more than 1,000 changed `Library/...` files (`(+1037 more)`), and these cost tokens.
5. The workspace walker also logs dozens of `genome.router` EPERM errors for protected `~/Library` folders.

## Expected
When the first scan skips the home directory or the system root, the watcher should skip it too. The map should stay empty, so the system prompt stays stable and the cache holds.

## `.empryoignore` doesn't help the watcher
Adding `/Library/` to `~/.empryoignore` does not stop it. In `onFileChanged`, the ignore check only runs when the path also has a build or vendor directory in it (roughly `isBuildDirPath(p) && ignored(p)`). Any other path goes straight to the extension check and is reindexed. Saving `.empryoignore` triggers a rescan, but the `Library/...` rows the watcher already added stay in the index (521 still there after the rescan).

## Suggested fix
- In `onFileChanged`, skip changes when the project root is the home directory or the system root (the same check the first scan uses).
- Check `.empryoignore` for every watcher path, not only build-dir paths.
- When a rescan runs, remove rows that are now ignored.

## Workaround
Open a project folder instead of `~`. A config setting can't do it: for `~`, the project config is the same file as the global `~/.empryo/config.json`, so `genome: false` would turn the Genome off in every project.

title: OpenCode Go Responses-only models (Muse Spark 1.3, Grok 4.7) fail with Model does not support this protocol
body:
## Summary

In **Empryo 3.9.4-beta**, some OpenCode Go models appear to be routed through the wrong API protocol.

**Muse Spark 1.3 Contributor works in native OpenCode CLI**, but fails inside Empryo with:

`Advisor unavailable: Model does not support this protocol.`

## Environment

- Empryo: `3.9.4-beta`
- OS: Windows
- Provider: `opencode-go`
- Model: `muse-spark-1.3-contributor`
- Authentication: Working with other OpenCode Go models

## Steps to reproduce

1. Connect OpenCode Go in Empryo.
2. Select `opencode-go/muse-spark-1.3-contributor`.
3. Send `Reply only PONG`.
4. Observe the protocol error.
5. Switch to `opencode-go/gpt-6-luna` and repeat.
6. Confirm that GPT-6 Luna succeeds.
7. Run Muse Spark 1.3 in native OpenCode CLI; it works.

## Test results

| Model | Required protocol | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Muse Spark 1.3 Contributor | Responses API | FAIL |
| Muse Spark 1.2 Contributor | Responses API | FAIL |
| Grok 4.7 | Responses API | FAIL |
| GPT-6 Luna | Responses API | PASS |
| DeepSeek V4.1 Flash | Chat Completions | PASS |

## Suspected root cause

OpenCode Go provides different endpoints for different model protocols:

- `/inference/go/openai/v1/responses`
- `/inference/go/openai/v1/chat/completions`

The model catalog contains provider SDK metadata that distinguishes these protocols.

Our testing suggests Empryo may select the API protocol based on model-name heuristics rather than consistently following the model's provider metadata.

GPT-6 Luna and Muse Spark 1.3 both require Responses, but only GPT-6 Luna succeeds.

This is a suspected cause based on reproducible behavior, not a fully verified internal implementation detail.

## Custom provider limitation

We investigated the documented **Other / Custom Provider** configuration.

It appears to support Chat Completions without an explicit Responses API override.

Therefore, adding Muse as a custom provider does not solve the problem.

## Expected behavior

Empryo should select the correct API protocol for each model, regardless of its name.

Muse Spark 1.3 should work with the existing OpenCode Go integration without a custom proxy.

## Suggested fix

1. Honor the model's declared SDK/protocol metadata.
2. Route Responses-only models through the Responses API.
3. Preserve compatibility with Chat Completions models.
4. Consider exposing a protocol override for custom providers.
5. Add regression tests covering non-GPT Responses-only models.

Related issues: #137, #198, #27, #46.

Happy to help test a fix or provide additional sanitized diagnostics.

title: 3.10.0-beta: request per-command NODE_AUTH_TOKEN forwarding for private-package installs
body:
## Summary

In the inspected Empryo 3.10.0-beta installation on Linux, an exported `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` reaches the Empryo process but is absent from commands launched through the shell tool, including orchestration shell nodes. I could not find a supported, explicitly authorized way to forward this existing variable directly to a package-manager process for a selected command. These observations concern that historical installation; current releases have not been verified here.

This blocks private-package installation via npm/pnpm when the matching registry authentication is configured, for example through an `.npmrc` auth entry referencing `${NODE_AUTH_TOKEN}`. The environment variable alone does not configure registry authentication. The user's terminal and its child shell had the variable; the tool's child shell did not. Re-exporting the variable or restarting from the same terminal does not resolve the observed tool-process filtering.

A failed dependency installation can prevent a subsequent build; compilation itself does not require this token. This report does not diagnose unrelated authentication failures or CI publishing 403s: a credential's presence does not establish publishing permissions.

## Environment

- Empryo: `3.10.0-beta`
- Linux, fish
- `em` resolves to the installed Empryo executable

## Minimal reproduction (dummy value, no secret)

In fish, before launching Empryo:

```fish
set -gx NODE_AUTH_TOKEN test-placeholder-not-a-secret
/bin/sh -c 'if [ -n "$NODE_AUTH_TOKEN" ]; then echo PRESENT; else echo ABSENT; fi'
em
```

The external shell prints `PRESENT`. Ask Empryo to run the same presence-only check through its shell tool or an orchestration shell node. In the affected installation it reports `ABSENT`. Do not print actual token values.

## Investigation

Presence-only checks with the configured environment confirmed that Empryo received the variable while its spawned shell processes did not. Static inspection of the installed build found a fixed environment allowlist: `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` is not included, so it is filtered before the additional sensitive-name check. The inspected shell/orchestrate schemas do not expose an `env` option, and I found no corresponding supported configuration setting.

The documented file-privacy settings and MCP environment configuration concern different mechanisms. This report is specifically about shell/orchestrate; it does not claim all execution tools share the same policy. The diagnosed cause is the shell child-process environment construction, not Orchestrate mode itself.

## Expected behavior / request

The goal is for an authorized npm/pnpm child process to receive a variable already present in Empryo's environment and use the configured registry authentication—not for the model to read, see, or print the token.

Please document an existing supported mechanism, if there is one, or provide explicit user-approved, per-command credential forwarding for selected environment variable names. Suggested requirements:

- Deny by default; do not inherit all secrets.
- Require explicit user consent for the selected variable and the specific command.
- Forward values directly to the authorized child process without exposing them to the model or in command-line arguments; redact secrets from model-visible output, logs, and session artifacts.
- Explain when environment filtering prevents an authenticated operation.

If the restriction is intentional, actionable documentation would help users avoid repeated exports/restarts that cannot fix it. No filtering bypass or broad security disablement is requested.

No credentials, private registry URLs, or project data are included in this report.

title: Windows/WSL: clipboard daemon spins a CPU core after the session exits
body:
Pull requests are disabled on this repo, so the fix is on a fork branch: [itsHaddad/Empryo@fix/clipboard-daemon-eof-spin](https://github.com/itsHaddad/Empryo/compare/main...fix/clipboard-daemon-eof-spin) (one commit, two files).

## Problem

The Windows clipboard daemon (`WindowsClipboardDaemon`, `src/core/platform/clipboard.ts`) loops on `[Console]::In.ReadLine()` and only breaks on `QUIT`. `ReadLine()` returns `$null` at EOF. When a session ends without sending `QUIT` (window closed, crash, kill, or the WSL interop bridge exiting), the daemon spins one CPU core until reboot, one `powershell.exe` per ended session.

Observed on 3.9.4-beta and 3.10.0-beta (linux-x64 under WSL2, Windows 11): two leftover daemons, parent process gone, had each used 19.3 h of CPU in 19.5 h.

## Repro

Run the loop in `powershell.exe` with redirected stdin, then close stdin. It keeps running at ~98% of a core.

## Fix

```diff
-        "  if ($line -eq 'QUIT') { break }",
+        "  if ($null -eq $line -or $line -eq 'QUIT') { break }",
```

With this change the process exits as soon as stdin closes. The branch also adds a source-contract test next to the existing POSIX guard in `tests/platform-windows.test.ts`.

Optional follow-up: write `QUIT` and close stdin before `kill()` on exit (in v3, `dispose()` only calls `kill()`).

title: Subagents don't have access to skills
Image-heavy conversations incorrectly clamp output to 1,024 tokens
body:
## Summary

In image-heavy conversations, Empryo appears to count inline image data as ordinary text when calculating the remaining output budget. This causes it to incorrectly treat the context window as exhausted and limit responses to **1,024 tokens**, even when actual input usage is well below the context limit.

## Environment

- **Version:** Empryo 3.10.1-beta
- **Operating system:** Windows 11
- **Model:** `claude-opus-5-5`
- **Context window:** 1,000,000 tokens
- **Model output limit in cached metadata:** 128,000 tokens

## Observed Behavior

- Responses terminate early with `finish_reason=length`.
- Empryo attempts both automatic continuations, but they are also affected.
- Some calls exhaust their output allowance without producing a visible answer.
- Individual calls stop at exactly **1,024 output tokens**.
- No explicit output-token limit was configured in the active global settings, project settings, or relevant environment variables.

## Recorded Measurements

For one affected request:

| Measurement | Value |
| :--- | ---: |
| Actual provider-reported input tokens | 275,099 |
| Full serialized request length, including inline image data | 4,098,632 characters |
| Attachment-aware request length | 993,368 characters |
| Input-token estimate using raw length in replay | 1,136,137 |
| Input-token estimate using attachment-aware length in replay | 275,361 |
| Resulting output allowance with existing code | 1,024 tokens |

The raw-length estimate incorrectly exceeds the **1,000,000-token context window**, while the attachment-aware estimate closely matches the provider-reported usage.

## Suspected Cause

Inspection of the installed bridge indicates that the normal output-budgeting path combines:

- A **raw serialized request length** that includes inline image data.
- A **characters-per-token ratio** calibrated using attachment-aware measurements.

These measurements use different accounting bases, inflating the estimated input-token count and triggering the built-in **1,024-token minimum output allowance**.

The relevant bundled code passes `B`, derived from `F.chars`, into the output-budget calculation:

```js
params: pOn(e, k, w, B)
```

The candidate correction tested in isolation uses the existing attachment-aware measurement:

```js
params: pOn(e, k, w, m$e(e, k))
```

These identifiers come from the bundled JavaScript in the installed bridge, not the original source.

## Offline Verification

The shipped middleware was replayed against **three recorded request snapshots**.

| Test | Result |
| :--- | :--- |
| Existing code | Output allowance clamped to 1,024 tokens in all three snapshots |
| Increased configured output limit | Still clamped to 1,024 tokens |
| Candidate attachment-aware correction | Output allowance restored to 128,000 tokens in all three snapshots |
| Streaming and non-streaming paths | Both reproduced the issue and the corrected result |
| Control with equal raw and attachment-aware lengths | Both versions preserved the 128,000-token allowance |

**Testing scope:** This was an offline replay of the installed middleware using recorded measurements. The candidate correction has not been applied to the installed app or verified end-to-end against the provider.

## Expected Behavior

Output budgeting should use consistent, attachment-aware token accounting. Inline image data should not be treated as ordinary text in a way that prematurely exhausts the estimated context window.

```
router.checkout-missing: /home/arti/Proyectos/Epsilon/\\wsl.localhost\Ubuntu\home\arti\Proyectos\Fixes: ENOENT: no such file or directory, realpath '/home/arti/Proyectos/Epsilon/\\wsl.localhost\Ubuntu\home\arti\Proyectos\Fixes'
```

In both cases the engine receives the raw Windows path. On Linux it is not an absolute path, so it is joined to the current workspace and `realpath` fails.

## Expected behavior

- Case B should open. The FAQ says folders opened through `\\wsl.localhost\<distro>\…` run inside that distro: https://empryo.com/docs/faq#can-the-desktop-app-open-a-repo-that-lives-in-wsl
- Case A should either open with the Windows engine or show a clear message. It should not produce a joined path.

## Suspected cause

I could not read the engine source (compiled build), so this is an inference from the error text. The UNC-to-Linux translation (`\\wsl.localhost\<distro>\a\b` → `/a/b`, and `C:\x` → `/mnt/c/x` or a switch to the Windows engine) seems to run only when a workspace is opened from scratch. It does not run when a tab is created from a workspace whose engine already runs in WSL. The path then reaches `router` untranslated.

## Workaround

None found yet. I have not verified that typing a WSL path (`/mnt/c/...` or `/home/...`) works, because the folder picker returns Windows paths.

title: Feature request: AI-assisted Routing setup using authenticated accounts
body:
Hi! Thanks for all the work on Empryo. The per-role controls in **Routing** are really useful, and I would love to suggest an optional way to make configuring them easier.

## Feature request

Could Routing offer a **“Suggest routing with AI”** or **“Auto-configure with AI”** action that recommends model assignments for each role, using **only the models available through the user's already-authenticated accounts/providers**?

The idea is to let AI help configure the role-to-model mapping, rather than requiring users to keep track of every model's strengths and manually choose one for each role. This would complement manual configuration and the **Best / Balanced / Frugal** presets, not replace them.

## Why this would help

When several providers or accounts are connected, it can be difficult to decide which available model fits Chat, Coders, Explorers, Code review, and the other roles. The most suitable configuration may also change when the user connects another account or gains access to new models.

An account-aware recommendation could help users make better use of the access they already have, without recommending models they cannot actually select.

## Possible experience

1. Click **Suggest routing with AI** in the Routing settings.
2. Choose a goal such as **quality first**, **balanced**, or **lower cost / faster responses**, optionally adding a short instruction.
3. Have the AI propose an available provider/account and model for each role, with a supported effort level where applicable and a brief explanation of each choice. Distinguish account choices only where Empryo exposes that control.
4. Preview the proposed changes, adjust any recommendation, and explicitly apply them to the desired **This tab / Project / Global** scope. Preserve manual choices the user wants to keep and the existing scope precedence.
5. Allow users to request a fresh suggestion after their available models change, without silently replacing their configuration.

## Example suggestions

These are illustrative strategies, not fixed model rankings:

- **Balanced:** suggest a capable reasoning model for **Chat**, a strong coding model for **Coders**, a model suited to careful checking for **Code review**, and faster models for **Explorers / Solo explorer**. Consider suitable lightweight options for **Marionette** and **Cleanup** when those roles are enabled, while ensuring **Web research** can use the required tools.
- **Quality first:** prioritize coding and review quality over latency, using higher effort only where the selected model supports it. An example instruction could be: *“Prioritize correctness for Coders and Code review, but keep exploration responsive.”*
- **Use my existing subscriptions:** *“Only use models from my signed-in subscription accounts; exclude metered API providers.”* If the app cannot reliably determine billing or entitlement details, let the user select the allowed accounts instead of guessing.

## Keeping it predictable

- Make this opt-in and keep manual routing fully available. An on-demand setup assistant would already be useful; this does not need to become a per-message routing system.
- Ground recommendations in the current selectable-model catalog and known capabilities, rather than invented model IDs or unsupported effort settings. Avoid presenting uncertain pricing or performance assumptions as facts.
- Use only the metadata needed for the recommendation; do not send authentication tokens or account secrets to the model making the suggestion.
- Suggest assignments for optional roles without turning those roles on automatically.

Would something along these lines fit the direction of Routing? The UI and exact selection criteria are just suggestions—I'd be happy with any approach that makes it easier to configure the roles intelligently from the models already available to the user. Thanks for considering it!

title: 3.12.4-beta: bump @ai-sdk/mcp to >=2.0.84 — subagent MCP calls still throw on non-object tool output
body:
## Summary

Every MCP tool call made from a subagent fails immediately with:

```
t is not an Object. (evaluating '"content"in t')
```

The cause is fixed upstream in `@ai-sdk/mcp@2.0.84`, released 2026-10-24. Empryo 3.12.4-beta still bundles **2.0.80**, so the fix is not reaching users. This is a patch-level dependency bump with no API change.

## Environment

- Empryo 3.12.4-beta, desktop, macOS arm64 (bridge built 2026-11-03)
- Also reproduced on 3.10.2-beta and 3.12.0-beta

## Steps to reproduce

1. Dispatch any subagent with a task that makes one MCP call, e.g.:

```
dispatch(tasks:[{agent:"orch-recon", task:"Call mcp__github__search_repositories with query 'empryo' and limit 1, then reply DONE."}])
```

2. The dispatch fails in one attempt, zero steps completed.

## Scope

Reproduced against four unrelated MCP servers, so this is not server-specific:

| tool | result |
|---|---|
| `mcp__github__search_repositories` | fails |
| `mcp__azure-devops__core_list_projects` | fails |
| `mcp__mcp-atlassian__jira_get_all_projects` | fails |
| `mcp__playwright__browser_tabs` | fails |

## Control

The identical `mcp__github__search_repositories` call from the main agent returns cleanly. Non-MCP tools (`read`, `grep`, `shell`, `web_search`) work fine in subagents. MCP tools are the only ones carrying `toModelOutput`, which isolates the failure to the MCP converter.

## Ruled out

- Non-streaming generation (`subagentStreamProviders: []`) — still fails.
- Full tool loading (`agentFeatures.toolLoading: "all"`) — still fails.

## Root cause

`mcpToModelOutput` uses the `in` operator before checking that its input is an object. `in` throws a `TypeError` on any non-object, so the guard meant to fall back to JSON is itself what crashes.

In the 3.12.4-beta bridge:

```js
function avr({output:e}){let t=e;if(!("content"in t)||!Array.isArray(t.content))return{type:"json",value:t};...}
```

The SDK's own dispatcher already handles non-objects for every tool *without* a converter:

```js
if(n?.toModelOutput) return await n.toModelOutput({toolCallId:e,input:t,output:u});
return typeof u==="string"?{type:"text",value:u}:{type:"json",value:dkn(u)}
```

So the MCP converter is the one outlier.

## Upstream fix

- **vercel/ai#23825** — the upstream report.
- **vercel/ai#23935** — "fix(mcp): handle primitive and nullish tool outputs", merged 2026-10-23.
- Released in **`@ai-sdk/mcp@2.0.84`** on 2026-10-24. Changelog: *"Fix MCP tool output conversion throwing on primitive or nullish results returned by output schemas or execute wrappers."*

The fix adds a string→text branch and a nullish guard:

```ts
if (typeof output === 'string') return { type: 'text', value: output };
if (output == null || typeof output !== 'object' || !('content' in output) || ...) {
  return { type: 'json', value: (output ?? null) as JSONValue };
}
```

It includes a regression test for a wrapped `execute` returning a string — the subagent case.

## Version fingerprint

The bundled `@ai-sdk/mcp` version, by feature presence in `empryo-bridge`:

| marker | landed | 3.10.2 | 3.12.0 | 3.12.4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `experimental_events` | 2.0.70 | yes | yes | yes |
| `createAdapter` | 2.0.73 | yes | yes | yes |
| SSE `responseBody` | 2.0.79 | yes | yes | yes |
| `validateAuthorizationServerURL` | 2.0.80 | yes | yes | yes |
| `waitsForProtocolVersionDiscovery` | 2.0.81 | no | no | no |
| string→text converter | 2.0.84 | no | no | no |

The pin is **2.0.80** across all three releases. Three releases have shipped since the fix was published (3.12.0 on Oct 27, 3.12.2 on Oct 31, 3.12.4 on Nov 3) without moving it.

## Request

Bump `@ai-sdk/mcp` to `>=2.0.84` in the 3.x dependency set. Patch-level, no API change, no migration.

## Verification after the bump

```bash
strings /Applications/Empryo.app/Contents/Resources/empryo-bridge | grep -c 'typeof output==="string"'
```

Non-zero means the fix is in. Then re-run the repro above — the dispatch should complete.

title: Approval prompt shows "/" for unexpanded variables and labels reads as writes
body:
**Version:** empryo 3.12.6-beta, macOS 26.7.1 (arm64), desktop app
**Area:** outside-cwd approval gate for the `shell` tool

### Bug 1 — unexpanded variables resolve to `/`
The agent ran (cwd = repo root):

    cat > $EMPRYO_TMP/script.py <<'EOF2' … EOF2
    cd $EMPRYO_TMP && uv run … python script.py

`$EMPRYO_TMP` = `<repo>/.empryo/tmp/tabs/<tab-id>`, i.e. **inside** the project.
The gate does not expand the variable, treats it as empty and reports:

    Denied: shell outside the project directory → /

The user sees a request to write to the filesystem root and, naturally, denies it.

**Expected:** expand at least `$EMPRYO_TMP`, `$HOME`, `~` (ideally any variable in the agent's environment) before classifying. Paths inside the cwd or the tab's own tmp dir should not prompt. If a path can't be resolved, show the raw token (`$EMPRYO_TMP/script.py`) rather than `/`.

### Bug 2 — a read-only command is presented as a write
    K=~/.config/some-app/key.json
    python3 -I - "$K" <<'EOF2'   # only open(sys.argv[1]) for reading
    …
    openssl dgst -sha256 -sign <(python3 -c "…open(sys.argv[1])…" "$K")

Nothing is written outside the project, yet the prompt asked the user to allow a **write** to `~/.config/some-app/key.json`. A shell variable assignment (`K=<path>`) appears to be classified as a write.

**Expected:** variable assignments, arguments, `<` input redirection and `<(…)` process substitution are reads; only `>`, `>>`, `tee`, `cp`/`mv` targets, `rm` and similar are writes.

### Bug 3 (UX) — the prompt doesn't say read vs write
Show the action (read / write / delete) and the exact resolved path per file the command touches, so users can allow reads while refusing writes.

### Feature request
`approvals.outsideCwd` is all-or-nothing (`ask|allow`). Please add a read-only allowlist, e.g. `approvals.readPaths: ["~/.config/some-app"]`, separate from writes.

title: fix: let cursor subscription models run shell in subagents
body:
## Summary

Models from a Cursor subscription cannot run terminal commands when Empryo uses them as subagents. Most of them fail every tool call, and the ones that recover waste several calls per task. People who pay for Cursor cannot use it to share the load of multi-agent workflows with their other plans.

## Context

Environment: Empryo desktop `3.12.7~beta` (also seen on `3.12.1~beta`), Linux x64, Cursor plan signed in through `/login cursor`, subagents started with `dispatch` (role `code` and `explore`), smoke task: run `git log -1 --oneline`, run `gh issue view <n>`, read one line of a file.

Results per model:

| Model | Shell | Read | Outcome |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `subscriptions/cursor/composer-2.5` | native `Shell` refused, then Empryo `shell` works | yes | completes after a few wasted calls |
| `subscriptions/cursor/gemini-4-argon` | `cursor_bash` fails, then Empryo `shell` works | yes | completes after a few wasted calls |
| `subscriptions/cursor/gemini-3.8-flash` | refused | yes | stops after 6 identical failures |
| `subscriptions/cursor/grok-4.7` | fails | fails | no tool call succeeds |
| `subscriptions/cursor/claude-haiku-5-5` | fails | fails | no tool call succeeds |
| `subscriptions/cursor/kimi-k2.7-code` | fails | fails | no tool call succeeds |
| `subscriptions/cursor/cursor-grok-4.6` | fails ~39 times | eventually | completes, with heavy waste |

Errors seen, verbatim:

- `refused: running shell commands is not enabled for this lane — the tools advertised to you are the ones available`
- `AI_NoSuchToolError: Model tried to call unavailable tool 'cursor_bash'. Available tools: read, grep, navigate, project, edit_file, multi_edit, refactor, shell, ...` (same for `cursor_read`)
- After that, calls to the advertised `shell`, `read` and `run_tool` from Grok 4.7 return `Tool not available`.
- `Read` with an absolute path returns `refused: <path> is outside the workspace`.

Likely cause, from the shipped `resources/empryo-bridge` of 3.12.7~beta: the Cursor exec handlers are created with `allowShell: t.allowShell??!1` (and `e.allowShell??!1`), and no caller passes an exec policy that enables it, so Cursor's native shell exec is always rejected. The models are also steered towards `cursor_bash` / `cursor_read`, which are not on the subagent tool belt.

For comparison, the same models through Cursor's own CLI (`cursor-agent -p --model composer-2.5` and `--model grok-4.7-medium`) run git, gh and vitest in the same repository with no errors, so the account and the models are able to use a shell.

No existing issue covers this; the closest are #59 (subagents could not read) and #240 (Grok 4.7 through OpenCode Go).

## Proposal

- Enable Cursor's native shell exec for subagent lanes that have shell permission (pass `allowShell: true` in the exec policy, honouring the same approval gates as Empryo's `shell` tool), or map native `Shell` / `Read` exec requests onto Empryo's `shell` and `read` tools.
- Stop advertising or steering towards `cursor_bash` / `cursor_read` when they are not on the belt, so models call the tools that exist.
- [ASSUMPTION] Absolute paths inside the workspace or its git worktrees should be readable, as with other providers.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A `dispatch` on `subscriptions/cursor/composer-2.5` runs `git log -1 --oneline` on its first shell call, with no `refused` or `AI_NoSuchToolError` in the run.
- [ ] The same task completes on `subscriptions/cursor/grok-4.7`, `subscriptions/cursor/claude-haiku-5-5` and `subscriptions/cursor/kimi-k2.7-code`.
- [ ] A read-only subagent (`explore`) on a Cursor model still cannot run shell or edit files.
- [ ] Shell commands from Cursor models go through the same approval rules as Empryo's `shell` tool.

## Out of scope

- `subscriptions/cursor/gpt-5.6-luna` fails with `Connect error not_found`, which looks like a model not available on the account rather than this bug.

title: fix: align subagent tool references when dispatch role is explore
body:
## Summary

Project agents defined with `mode: code` but no explicit `tools:` list fail immediately when `dispatch` omits `role: "code"` (the default role is `explore`). The parent chat and every affected subagent see a hard failure before the model runs any real work.

## Context

Environment: Empryo desktop **3.12.8-beta** (engine registry `version: "3.12.8-beta"`, Linux x64), Anthropic models via subscription (`claude-opus-5-5`, `claude-sonnet-5-5`), project agents in `.empryo/agents/*.md` with `mode: code` and **no** `tools:` line (`frontend`, `qa`, `docs`, `devops`). Parent orchestrator calls `dispatch(tasks: [{ task: "…", agent: "frontend" }])` without `role`.

**Error (verbatim):**

`Failed after 1 attempt. Last error: Tool reference 'agent_send' not found in available tools`

Logged at `~/.empryo/logs/errors.jsonl`, e.g. `2026-11-14T02:10:26.734Z`, `surface: "desktop-bridge"`, `source: "agent-error"`, message `agent-1 stream: HTTP 400 — Tool reference 'agent_send' not found in available tools`.

**What still works**

- Same agent and task with `role: "code"` completes (smoke: reply `OK`).
- Agents that declare `tools:` in front matter (`architect`, `issue-writer`, `code-reviewer`, `security-auditor`) dispatch without `role` and do not hit this error.

**An explicit `tools:` allowlist does not work around it**

Adding `tools: read, find, grep, navigate, analyze, genome_query, genome_impact, edit_file, ast_edit, project, shell, shell_jobs, web_search, computer_batch, computer_observe, computer_targets` (no `skills`) to `frontend` and `qa` only changes the name in the error: dispatched without `role`, both fail with `Tool reference 'skills' not found in available tools`, and still succeed with `role: "code"`. A copy of the agent without `mode: code` and with a similar list (`read, grep, navigate, genome_query, edit_file, ast_edit, project, shell, shell_jobs, computer_batch, computer_observe, computer_targets`) dispatched without `role` succeeds, and one that also lists `skills` fails with `Tool reference 'profiles' not found in available tools`. The same definitions on `subscriptions/cursor/composer-2.5` (`docs`, `devops`) do not fail in any combination, which suggests only the Anthropic request validates tool references.

**Likely cause**

For `explore` (or default) role, Empryo strips subagent-steering tools such as `agent_send` from the tool belt exposed to the child, but the request to the provider still includes **tool references** to those names. Anthropic returns HTTP 400 when a referenced tool is not in the available set. The failure is not in the project agent markdown body; it is in how Empryo builds the child session when `mode: code` agents are launched without `role: "code"`.

**Related prior signal**

Same pattern with `background_await` on `2026-10-31` and `2026-11-13T00:22:08Z` in the same `errors.jsonl` (research / generic explore lane).

**Reproduction (minimal)**

1. In any repo, define `.empryo/agents/frontend.md` with `mode: code`, no `tools:` (stock template).
2. From main chat: `dispatch(tasks: [{ task: "Reply OK.", agent: "frontend" }])` — omit `role`.
3. Observe immediate dispatch failure with `agent_send` not found.
4. Repeat with `role: "code"` — succeeds.

## Proposal

1. When resolving tools for a dispatched subagent, **do not emit tool references** for tools that are not on that lane’s belt (including `agent_send`, `background_dispatch`, `background_await`, `profiles`, etc.).
2. **Or** treat `mode: code` in the agent definition as implying `role: "code"` when `role` is omitted, so the full code belt matches references.
3. Document in agent / dispatch docs that callers must pass `role: "code"` for implementer agents until (1) or (2) ships.
4. [ASSUMPTION] Child agents with an explicit `tools:` list should only receive references to tools on that list; today a `mode: code` definition still gets a reference to `skills`, and listing `skills` adds one to `profiles`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `dispatch` with `agent: "frontend"` and **no** `role`, on an agent definition with `mode: code` and no `tools:`, completes a smoke task without HTTP 400.
- [ ] No tool reference appears in the provider request unless the tool is on the child’s effective belt (explore vs code).
- [ ] `dispatch` with `role: "explore"` on a read-only agent still cannot call `edit_file` or `shell` (no regression).
- [ ] Regression test or internal fixture: child request schema contains no dangling `tool_reference` entries.

## Out of scope

- Cursor subscription shell routing (#261) — separate issue.

title: Belt integrity: tools reach the model without inputSchema ("rebuilt with a spread — use deriveTool")
body:
## Summary

The engine logs a recurring `belt` integrity error: a set of tools reaches the model **without an `inputSchema`**. The log message itself points at the cause ("A tool object was rebuilt with a spread — use deriveTool").

```
{"surface":"desktop-bridge","source":"belt","message":"Belt integrity: memory, dispatch, agent_send, agent_create, background_dispatch, background_status, background_stop, background_await, rename_tab, browser, find_agent reached the model with no inputSchema (subscriptions/claude-opus-5-5). A tool object was rebuilt with a spread — use deriveTool."}
```

## Scope (from `~/.empryo/logs/errors.jsonl`)

- **421 occurrences** between 2026-10-30 and 2026-11-17.
- Surfaces: `headless` (371), `desktop-bridge` (50).
- Models: `subscriptions/claude-sonnet-5-5` (407), `subscriptions/claude-opus-5-5` (8), `subscriptions/claude-haiku-5-5` (5), and one with no model (`none`).
- Affected tools: `memory`, `dispatch`, `agent_send`, `agent_create`, `background_dispatch`, `background_status`, `background_stop`, `background_await`, `rename_tab`, `browser`, `find_agent`. One variant lists only `memory, browser`.

## Expected

Every tool on the belt is sent with its `inputSchema`.

## Impact

Without a schema the model has to guess the arguments for delegation (`dispatch`, `background_*`, `agent_*`), `memory` and `browser`. This can cause failed calls and retries, or the model skipping delegation entirely and doing the work itself, which defeats the task-router setup.

## Environment

- Empryo 3.13.0-beta (also seen on 3.12.x), desktop app on macOS arm64.
- Providers: Claude and ChatGPT subscriptions plus Cursor, all signed in through `/login`.
- `agentFeatures.toolLoading`: default (`auto`).

title: LSP install on macOS: servers go into ~/package.json, exit 127 without system node, and lsp status is wrong
body:
## Summary

On macOS, installing language servers from the desktop **Language servers** panel (and `empryo lsp install`) reports success but leaves Empryo without working servers. Three separate problems:

### 1. npm servers are installed into the user's home `package.json`, not `~/.empryo/lsp-servers/`

The installer runs `bun add` in `~/.empryo/lsp-servers/`, but that folder has no `package.json`. Bun walks up to the nearest ancestor manifest, `~/package.json`, adds the servers there, and installs them into `~/node_modules`. The install prints `✓ vtsls installed` and `~/.empryo/lsp-servers/` stays empty.

```
$ empryo lsp install vtsls
Installing @vtsls/language-server@0.3.0 via bun...
bun add v1.4.4
installed @vtsls/language-server@0.3.0 with binaries:
 - vtsls
✓ vtsls installed
$ ls ~/.empryo/lsp-servers      # empty
$ cat ~/package.json            # now lists @vtsls/language-server, vscode-langservers-extracted, ...
```

**Workaround:** create `~/.empryo/lsp-servers/package.json` (`{"name":"empryo-lsp-servers","private":true}`) and install again. The servers then land in `~/.empryo/lsp-servers/node_modules`.

**Expected:** the installer creates its own manifest (or passes `--cwd` with a manifest) so it never touches a parent `package.json`.

### 2. npm servers exit 127 when Node comes from nvm

The installed servers start with `#!/usr/bin/env node`. With Node from nvm (`~/.nvm/versions/node/...`), the environment used to spawn servers has no `node`:

```
$ empryo lsp health
✗ typescript  ~/.empryo/lsp-servers/node_modules/.bin/vscode-eslint-language-server — LSP server exited with code 127
✗ json        ~/.empryo/lsp-servers/node_modules/.bin/vscode-json-language-server — LSP server exited with code 127
✗ yaml        ~/.empryo/lsp-servers/node_modules/.bin/yaml-language-server — LSP server exited with code 127
```

The same missing `node` breaks Claude Code plugin hooks run by Empryo (`sh: node: command not found`). MCP servers do get the shell `PATH` (the docs say tools from nvm/Homebrew are found), but LSP servers and hooks do not.

**Workaround:** symlink `node` into a directory on the default `PATH` (`/opt/homebrew/bin/node`). After that `empryo lsp health` passes, and after a restart the desktop resolves `safeReturnPath` to 32 references in 11 files over `lsp`, instead of 2 references in 1 file over the `ts-morph` fallback.

**Expected:** spawn LSP servers (and hooks) with the same shell `PATH` MCP servers get, or run Node servers with the bundled runtime.

### 3. `empryo lsp status` says "no server installed" while `health` passes

With the servers installed and `empryo lsp health` showing handshakes OK for typescript/json/yaml, `empryo lsp status` still prints `no server installed` for every language.

## Impact

The install UI reports success, so users believe they have full code intelligence while Empryo silently falls back to `ts-morph`. Cross-file references, call hierarchy and post-edit diagnostics are incomplete, and the installer modifies an unrelated `~/package.json`.

## Environment

- Empryo 3.13.1-beta (desktop + CLI), macOS arm64
- Node via nvm (v26.x), no system Node
- Packages: `vtsls`, `eslint-lsp`, `tailwindcss-language-server`, `json-lsp`, `yaml-language-server`

title: Desktop lists dead engine registries as running, and Stop cannot dismiss them
body:
On Windows, Empryo 3.13.0-beta reported that engines were running with no window, and the in-app update would not proceed. Those engines were not running.

%LOCALAPPDATA%\Empryo\engines still had nine registry files after the engines had exited. Their logs already contained engine.terminate. No empryo-engine-* named pipes remained. Eight of the recorded PIDs were dead. The ninth had been reused by an unrelated Python process, so a PID-only check showed it as alive. The registries covered several projects and older builds (3.10.0-beta through 3.13.0-beta). There was no window to close, and Stop had nothing to talk to.

Expected: a registry whose process is gone is not shown as running, and it does not block an update. Stop either dismisses it or the app removes it on its own.

Actual: the desktop counted those rows as engines running with no window. Stop could not clear a registry key whose pipe was already gone.

This is separate from the 3.13.1-beta note that a stopped helper is no longer reported as still running. That note is the cells helper. The banner is still in the 3.13.1 bundle: a registry row with no parent and no clients is counted as running with no window. The 3.13.1 updater checks that the PID's program is Empryo before it discards a staged update, so a dead or reused PID shouldn't, by itself, block the install. The banner can still be stuck.

Clearing the dead registry files, leaving the logs and the project sessions, let 3.13.1-beta install.

title: Windows Desktop chat typing lags, then catches up, while the main thread is busy or stalled
body:
On Windows, Empryo 3.13.1-beta desktop, typing in the chat lags, then the characters appear in a burst, then it lags again. The machine was not CPU- or memory-bound: about 2% CPU, about 24 GB free of 62 GB.

The unsuffixed Empryo process had one thread at about 100% of a core for the whole sample. The chat renderer was also busy, at about 35–75% of a core. The samples were inside Empryo.exe.

The log already records the other shape of the same hitch. The main thread was blocked for about 2.4 s and about 1.6 s during invoke git.status. In the longer one, the process used 0 ms of CPU, so it was paused or starved, not busy. Either shape queues keystrokes and then flushes them.

This is separate from a dead engine registry being shown as running, and from Remove refusing the main checkout.

title: Engine OOMs inside keepalive.state and blocks the model switch (3.14.0-beta, Windows)
body:
## Summary

On Empryo 3.14.0-beta (Windows 11 x64), one engine process grew its resident
memory from 846 MB to 4574 MB in about ten seconds while handling
`keepalive.state`, then threw `RangeError: Out of memory`. The same failure
surfaced in the TUI events panel as a failed model switch, and the
cache-lifetime probe timed out, so the header shows "Cache TTL unknown".

This is not the machine running out of RAM. The host has 61.7 GB installed
and had roughly 20 GB free at the time; the process peaked at 4.4 GB. V8
hit its own heap limit while the OS still had memory to spare.

## What the user sees

TUI events panel, all from one incident:

- `RangeError: Out of memory` (twice)
- `Error — Could not change the model: model: Out of memory.`
- `Cache TTL unknown` in the header
- 
The model switch was rolled back, so the header still shows the previous
model (Kimi Code-sub / Kimi K3.1 Pro).

## Timeline (UTC, 2026-11-20)

| Time | PID | Surface | Source | Message |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 07:31:00 | 55460 | tui | tui/keepalive | TimeoutError |
| 07:31:25 | 55460 | tui | tui/engine-resync | quiet: no answer in 5s |
| 07:32:26 | 55460 | tui | tui/cache-lifetime | no answer in 1m |
| 07:33:28.199 | 76028 | desktop-bridge | event-loop-stall | main thread blocked ~151628 ms during `invoke keepalive.state`; process used 274141 ms of CPU |
| 07:33:28.204 | 76028 | desktop-bridge | memory-spike | peak memory rose from 846 MB to 4574 MB within 10 s (now 4357 MB) during `invoke keepalive.state` |
| 07:33:28.492 | 76028 | desktop-bridge | model:subscriptions/kimi-code/k3.1-pro | RangeError: Out of memory |
| 07:33:29.064 | 76028 | desktop-bridge | session-log | append(assistant) failed: Out of memory — this turn is not persisted |
| 08:21:01 | 55460 | tui | engine | RangeError: Out of memory |

From `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Empryo\logs\errors.jsonl`, lines 2002–2010.

## Process state after the spike

PID 76028 is still alive and did not recover its memory
(`logs/live/76028.json`, beat 09:52 UTC):

- version 3.14.0-beta, win32 x64, host DESKTOP-PE75QAG
- started 02:31:08 UTC, so it had been up ~5 h before the spike
- RSS 317 MB, peakRSS 4357 MB, heap 1221 MB
- arrayBuffers 569 MB, external 1159 MB, mimalloc committed ~2300 MB
- 1,208,704 live objects
- idle collector ran once and freed 5 MB

## How the model-switch message is produced

`tab.setModel` sets the new model ID and then awaits `rebuildTabAgent`.
`rebuildTabAgentNow` allocates the replacement agent; that allocation throws
`RangeError: Out of memory`. The handler catches it, restores the previous
model ID and rethrows, and the TUI reports it through
`tui.use-chat.engine-change-failed` ("Could not change the {what}: {reason}"),
which is why the text reads `model: Out of memory`. The model and provider
are not at fault; the same process also failed to append the assistant turn
to the session log for the same reason.

"Cache TTL unknown" is the fallback label (`common.cache-ttl-unknown`) shown
when the `cache.lifetime` probe gets no answer and no previous snapshot
exists. Here it got no answer because the main thread was blocked.

## Environment

- Empryo 3.14.0-beta (release date 2026-11-19), Windows desktop bridge + TUI
- Windows 11 x64, 61.7 GB RAM, ~20 GB free — OS memory pressure was not a factor
- Model in use: `subscriptions/kimi-code/k3.1-pro.`

## Notes

- `keepalive.state` is a recurring stall point on this machine, not just this
  incident. The same source accounts for multi-minute main-thread blocks on
  earlier days (e.g. 2026-11-07, PID 63696, ~45 s, reported as blocked with no
  CPU time). Today's case is the first that also exhausted the heap.
- The 151 s stall here burned 274 s of CPU, so it was a real computation or
  allocation storm, not a wait on I/O.

title: Cleanup ledger grows to 19 GB in ~32h with 2,000+ 60s event-loop stalls on keepalive.state (Windows beta)
body:
## Summary

On Windows (VMware VM, 4 vCPU / 12 GB RAM), Empryo beta sessions repeatedly blocked the desktop-bridge main thread in `invoke keepalive.state` for 50–64 seconds at a time, and one session (PID 9756) wrote a **19.35 GB** `cleanup-ledger` JSONL file in ~32 hours. Across 16 days the log recorded **2,384** `event-loop-stall` events and 5 `[silent-exit]` TUI crash reports. The machine became noticeably slow while these sessions were active; it is idle now that they have exited.

This looks related to but distinct from #271 (V8 OOM inside `keepalive.state`): here the dominant symptom is an unbounded write volume to the cleanup ledger plus CPU-bound stalls, with no `memory-spike` events in our log.

## Environment

- Empryo **3.12.7-beta / 3.12.8-beta** in the crash reports (current installed binary is 3.14.1-beta, installed after most events)
- Windows Server 2022 x64, VMware virtual machine, 4 vCPU, 12 GB RAM
- `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Empryo` and `%USERPROFILE%\.empryo` on the system drive

## Evidence

### 1. Cleanup ledger growth

`%USERPROFILE%\.empryo\cleanup-ledger\` contains 9 files, 22.68 GB total:

| File | Size | Created | Last write | PID |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `edits-9756-mwaspglz.jsonl` | **19.35 GB** | 2026-11-10 06:38 | 2026-11-11 15:12 | 9756 |
| `edits-13328-mwggxskn.jsonl` | 1.79 GB | 2026-11-14 05:55 | 2026-11-14 09:32 | 13328 |
| `edits-14956-mwrwo5w7.jsonl` | 1.32 GB | 2026-11-22 06:01 | 2026-11-22 08:13 | 14956 |
| 6 smaller files | 0.3 GB total | 2026-11-06 → 11-22 | — | — |

- The 19.35 GB file is ~**96 million lines** (~215 bytes/line), ~54 million path entries, ~44% duplicates.
- Every entry is metadata only, e.g. `{"k":"e","p":"c:/users/.../temp/2/.../venv/lib/site-packages/uvicorn/config.py","t":null,"h":"290873116282709081","s":0,"b":"unknown"}` — `s` is always `0`, `b` always `"unknown"`.
- In a 50k-line sample, ~66% of paths point into `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp` (mostly a deleted RDPMonitor-audit venv that was walked repeatedly), ~25% into `%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes` cache/scratch.
- There is no size cap, rotation, or retention visible: `.empryo\config.json` only contains `{"yolo": true}`. A stale `genome-writer.lock.holder.14956...` file remains after the writer died.

### 2. Event-loop stalls (same PIDs that wrote the ledgers)

From `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Empryo\logs\errors.jsonl` (2,527 lines; 2,384 are `event-loop-stall`):

| PID | Stalls | Max blocked | Ledger file |
|---|---|---|---|
| 9756 | **2,003** | 63,722 ms (line 1630, `invoke keepalive.state`) | 19.35 GB |
| 13328 | 193 | 74,024 ms | 1.79 GB |
| 14956 | 130 | 61,867 ms (line 2473; CPU time 66,687 ms) | 1.32 GB |
| 11532 | 20 | 50,775 ms | 207 MB |
| 17776 | 29 | 10,648 ms | 14.5 MB |

Recent example, line 2527:
`{"ts":"2026-11-22T16:13:27.569Z","pid":14956,"surface":"desktop-bridge","source":"event-loop-stall","message":"main thread blocked ~59648ms (heartbeat overdue; this process used 64531ms of CPU) during: invoke github.pulls"}`

The stalls are CPU-bound (60+ seconds of CPU burned per block), not I/O waits. There are **0** `memory-spike` events in this log, so this is not the same OOM signature as #271.

### 3. Silent exits / suspected OOM kills

Five `[silent-exit]` crash reports in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Empryo\logs`, e.g. PID 13328 (2026-11-22): ran 3h 35m, RSS 997 MB / peak 1113 MB, 13 sandboxes spawned/terminated, no clean exit path — the report itself says "killed outright (an out-of-memory kill is the usual cause...)". PID 9756 crashed with RSS 710 MB / peak 877 MB after ~1d 8h.

## Impact

- System drive lost ~22 GB to metadata-only journals in ~2 weeks (63.7% full on a 200 GB drive).
- While sessions ran, the VM was continuously slow: repeated 60-second main-thread blocks with 50–65 s CPU burn each.
- TUI sessions died without clean shutdown, leaving stale lock files.

## Expected behavior

- Cleanup ledger should be bounded (size/count cap, rotation, deduplication, or async batched writes off the main thread), and old per-PID files should be pruned automatically.
- No single bookkeeping operation should block the desktop-bridge event loop for ~60 seconds repeatedly.

## Questions

1. What writes these `edits-<pid>-<id>.jsonl` files, and why can one session emit ~96 million entries?
2. Is there a supported config knob to disable or cap the cleanup ledger today?
3. Are these ledger writes on the main thread, and could they be batched/moved to a worker?

Related: #271 (`keepalive.state` OOM / stalls on 3.14.0-beta), #270 (Windows typing lag while main thread stalls).

title: Java LSP: support JDT LS virtual documents and dependency definitions via classFileContentsSupport
body:
**Environment:** Linux x86_64; Empryo Desktop 3.15.0-beta, standalone LSP backend; Eclipse JDT LS 1.63.0 (reports 1.63.0-SNAPSHOT in the handshake); Java 25.0.4.1. Maven project with org.springframework.boot:spring-boot:4.1.2 resolved.

**Minimal reproducible example:** Add Probe.java under a Maven source root:

java

```

import org.springframework.boot.SpringApplication;

class Probe {
    Class<?> dependency() { return SpringApplication.class; }
}

```
**Steps to reproduce:**

Open the Maven project in Empryo and wait for JDT LS to report Ready.
Run navigate with action: "definition", file set to Probe.java, and symbol: "SpringApplication".
As a control, request type information for SpringApplication using analyze(type_info).
Expected behavior: Go to Definition opens the declaration of SpringApplication from the Maven dependency.

Actual behavior: Go to Definition returns unsupported. Type information resolves the Spring class through LSP.

Confirmed technical findings: A direct JDT LS client received no dependency location when initializationOptions.extendedClientCapabilities.classFileContentsSupport was omitted. With the capability set to true, JDT LS returned a jdt:// location, and java/classFileContents returned the source. Project-local definitions resolved without the capability.

Suggested implementation direction: Advertise classFileContentsSupport when initializing JDT LS. Preserve jdt:// definition locations as virtual URIs, fetch their content through java/classFileContents, and open the virtual document at the returned range.

Acceptance criteria:

Empryo’s navigate(definition) resolves SpringApplication to its dependency declaration and can open the source at the returned location.
Project-local file:// definition navigation continues to work.

title: Java LSP: empty publishDiagnostics incorrectly reported as unavailable diagnostics backend
body:
**Environment:** Linux x86_64; Empryo Desktop 3.15.0-beta, standalone LSP backend; Eclipse JDT LS 1.63.0 (reports 1.63.0-SNAPSHOT in the handshake); Java 25.0.4.1; imported Maven project.

**Minimal reproducible example:** Add Probe.java under a Maven source root:

java

```

class Probe {
    int check() { return "wrong"; }
}

```
**Steps to reproduce:**

Wait for JDT LS to report Ready, then run analyze with action: "diagnostics" on Probe.java.
Confirm that the tool reports Type mismatch: cannot convert from String to int (16777235).
Change return "wrong"; to return 1;, save, and run diagnostics again after JDT LS reconciles the file.
Expected behavior: The second call succeeds and reports zero diagnostics. The previous error is cleared.

Actual behavior: The first call reports the type error through LSP. After the fix, the tool returns No diagnostics backend available (unsupported) instead of a successful empty result.

Confirmed technical findings: A direct JDT LS client received textDocument/publishDiagnostics with the type error, then a notification with diagnostics: [] after the fix. JDT LS did not advertise diagnosticProvider; a direct textDocument/diagnostic request returned UnsupportedOperationException. Empryo can surface nonempty push diagnostics, but its tool result does not distinguish the clean state from an unavailable backend.

Suggested implementation direction: Track an empty push result for the current document contents separately from “no publication received yet” and “no backend.” Clear cached errors on an empty publication and return a successful empty LSP result. Do not require pull diagnostics from a server that does not advertise them.

Acceptance criteria:

analyze(diagnostics) reports the type mismatch before the fix and succeeds with zero diagnostics after the server publishes an empty list.
The previous error is not retained after the empty publication.
A file awaiting its first publication is not reported as clean, and a clean file is not reported as unsupported.
Neither report was published.
